papers.abstract: Abstract Background Genetic mosaicism is a well-recognized consequence of CRISPR–Cas9 genome editing, yet its characterization remains challenging, especially when it involves low-frequency structural variants. A comprehensive analysis of mosaicism requires deep and unbiased sequencing of the target loci, with accurate single-molecule reads. Methods We performed amplification-free PureTarget PacBio sequencing to investigate CRISPR-Cas9 outcomes at on-target and off-target sites in genome edited zebrafish and their offspring. CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing was performed by micro-injection in fertilized eggs at the single-cell stage. Results Thirty samples from pooled larvae and individual zebrafish were successfully sequenced, resulting in > 1100x average target coverage. The PacBio reads reached an exceptional accuracy (QV39) over the target regions, with every read originating from a unique DNA molecule. The two haplotypes of the target loci displayed a balanced depth of coverage, while long-range PCR of the same samples resulted in skewed data. Further analysis of the PureTarget data revealed widespread genetic mosaicism in individual founder (F0) fish, with up to 18 distinct on-target events and 11 off-target events present in a single adult founder. Several CRISPR-Cas9 editing outcomes, including large structural variants and off-target mutations, were inherited to the F1 generation. Notably, as many as seven unique editing events were found among sibling F1 juvenile offspring derived from a single founder pair, thereby confirming the presence of genetic mosaicism in germ cells of founder zebrafish. This implies that some consequences of CRISPR-Cas9 editing may emerge only in the second generation. We also analyzed DNA methylation signals in the PureTarget data but did not observe altered 5mC CpG levels in genome edited samples. Conclusions PureTarget enables efficient, accurate, and unbiased profiling of genetic mosaicism and DNA methylation at pre-defined genomic regions. Our results show that CRISPR–Cas9–induced mosaicism is widespread and represents an important factor to consider in genome editing experiments.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Prolonged fasting may improve metabolic health, but controlled data in healthy adults with longer follow-up and multi-omics profiling are limited. We investigated the immediate and 12-week follow-up effects of a 5-day fasting intervention on body composition, gut microbiome, and circulating and fecal metabolites, and assessed whether baseline characteristics predict individual weight-loss response. Methods In a randomized, waitlist-controlled trial, 38 healthy adults completed a 5-day fasting intervention with 12-week follow-up (LEANER study). Outcomes included body mass index and body composition, gut microbiome composition, and plasma and fecal metabolites. Changes over time and between groups were evaluated using regression-based models and paired non-parametric tests, as appropriate. Additionally, permutation-based multivariate testing was performed on microbiome and metabolome data. Twelve-week body weight response was predicted using data-driven machine learning with cross-validation, followed by external validation in three independent cohorts undergoing prolonged fasting protocols. Results Fasting reduced body mass index acutely, predominantly driven by loss of fat mass, and these improvements partially persisted at 12 weeks. Fasting induced marked shifts in gut microbiome composition and in plasma and fecal metabolites. Post-fasting and longer-term changes in microbial diversity were associated with baseline microbiome diversity. A model combining baseline microbiome and clinical variables predicted body mass index response at 12 weeks; prominent predictors included an unclassified Faecalibacterium species, Oscillibacter sp. 50_27, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and systolic blood pressure. The model generalized to three independent cohorts, including individuals with metabolic syndrome, patients with multiple sclerosis exposed to repeated fasting, and healthy volunteers fasting for 6–12 days. Conclusions In healthy adults, a 5-day prolonged fasting intervention produces robust short-term metabolic changes with partial persistence and consistent remodeling of the gut microbiome and metabolite profiles. Baseline microbiome and clinical characteristics can help stratify expected longer-term responses, supporting the development of individualized fasting-based interventions. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04452916. Prospectively registered on June 29, 2020.

papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated gastric cancer (EBVaGC) is a molecularly distinct, highly immunogenic gastric cancer subtype, yet the role of tertiary lymphoid structure (TLS) during therapy remains unclear. Using a large locally advanced EBVaGC cohort (144 samples), combined with spatial transcriptomics (11 samples) and a single-cell atlas (77 samples), we show that EBVaGC exhibits enhanced TLS formation compared with EBV-negative gastric cancer, with invasive-margin TLS (IM-TLS) predicting favorable prognosis. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy disrupts TLS formation and shows limited efficacy in EBVaGC. Recurrent tumors display increased neutrophil infiltration around TLS, with aging neutrophils recruited via the CXCR4-CXCL12 axis. Mechanistically, chemotherapy induces EBV reactivation, activating neutrophil pattern recognition receptors and promoting neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, which impairs lymphocyte migration and TLS maturation. These findings identify EBV reactivation-driven neutrophil aging and NET formation as a mechanism underlying poor prognosis in EBVaGC, positioning IM-TLS as a prognostic biomarker and neutrophil dysfunction as a therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Mass spectrometry (MS)-based single-cell proteomics (SCP) enables proteome-wide analysis at single-cell resolution, offering insights into cellular heterogeneity, biological processes, and disease mechanisms. However, conventional nanoLC-MS workflows are constrained by long gradients and low throughput, limiting their application to small cohorts. Here, we present a multicolumn nanoLC-MS platform that achieves 5-minute separation windows with 100% duty cycles at ~100 nL/min, enabling the analysis of up to 288 single cells per day. The system provides stable peptide separation, negligible carryover, and robust retention-time reproducibility across nearly 1200 consecutive injections. We successfully analyze more than 4000 samples at nearly 288 samples per day (SPD) throughput. The platform identifies ~5000 proteins per 250 pg digest injection and an average of ~4000 proteins per single HeLa cell with maxima exceeding 5100, which is comparable to state-of-the-art longer-gradient workflows. Quantitative benchmarking with mixed-species standards confirm the quantitative accuracy is largely maintained during extended acquisition. Applying the workflow to 783 LPS-treated RAW264.7 macrophages reveals substantial cellular heterogeneity under a uniform inflammatory stimulus. Together, these results establish a robust and scalable platform for high-throughput SCP, enabling thousands of single-cell analyses within a single study while maintaining deep proteome coverage and biological interpretability.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma and depression frequently co-occur, yet the mechanisms linking them remain unclear. Here, we show that chronic stress, systemic inflammation, or neuropathic pain are associated with hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice. Chronic stress hyperactivates a glutamatergic paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus → cholinergic dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus → liver circuit, increasing intratumoral acetylcholine. Single-cell transcriptomics identifies acetylcholine-responsive Chrna9+ epithelial cells that interact with macrophages through COL1A1/2-CD44-STAT3 signaling to promote CXCL1 production. Acetylcholine also promotes tumor cell proliferation through CHRNA9. Circulating CXCL1 crosses the blood-brain barrier and activates hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons, exacerbating depression-like behaviors and establishing a liver-brain feedback loop. Silencing the hypothalamic vagal circuit, tumor-specific Chrna9 knockdown, or systemic CXCL1 neutralization restrains tumor progression and alleviates depression-like behaviors. These findings identify a neural and immune mechanism linking chronic stress to hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice.

papers.abstract: Race and ethnicity play an important role in breast cancer disparities; however, these variables are not consistently reported in research articles. Our study evaluates contemporary trends in racial and ethnic demographic reporting in clinical breast surgery research over a six-year period. PubMed search engine was queried for breast surgery related clinical research articles published from January 2017 to June 2023. The four breast journals with the highest impact factors were evaluated: Annals of Surgical Oncology, Breast Cancer Research and Treatment, Clinical Breast Cancer, and The Breast Journal. Statistical analyses were conducted using chi-square, Fisher's exact tests, or Cochran-Armitage Trend Test. Among 288 studies included, 181 (62.9%) reported any race/ethnicity. Studies were divided based on year of publication into three study periods: 2017-2018 (n = 108), 2019-2020 (n = 87), 2021-2023 (n = 93). Studies consistently reported White race across all time periods (100% vs. 96.4% vs. 100.0%) (p = 0.09), along with Black race (79.3% vs. 76.4% vs. 88.2%, p = 0.20), Asian race (50.0% vs. 45.5% vs. 60.3%, p = 0.24), Hispanic ethnicity (46.6% vs. 47.3 vs. 48.5%, p = 0.97), and "Other" race (55.2% vs. 61.8% vs. 66.2%, p = 0.45). Reporting of any race/ethnicity was found to have increased in recent years (53.7% vs. 63.2% vs. 73.1%, p < 0.01), only up to 73.1% in 2021-2023. Race reporting in high-impact breast surgery journals has increased significantly from 2017 to 2023, although only reaching 73.1% in 2021-2023. Specific populations, including Hispanics and Asian-Americans, remain underrepresented. While increasing, race reporting remains limited in clinical breast research, underscoring the need for more consistent and comprehensive research standards.

papers.abstract: Evidence is inconsistent regarding an association between alcohol consumption and survival following a breast cancer diagnosis; therefore, we examined how change in alcohol consumption affects all-cause mortality (ACM) in a population of breast cancer survivors. We prospectively assessed pre-diagnosis, pre- to post-diagnosis, and post-diagnosis change in alcohol consumption among 1,558 postmenopausal women (mean age-at-diagnosis: 71 years) diagnosed with non-metastatic invasive breast cancer from the American Cancer Society Cancer Prevention Study-II Nutrition Cohort (baseline: 1992-1993). Five categories of alcohol intake were determined at each assessment; change in alcohol consumption was categorized as stable, quit, reduced, and increased. Change occurred at a median of two years before (pre-diagnosis) and two years after (post-diagnosis) diagnosis. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to estimate adjusted hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for the associations between change groups and ACM. Over a median follow-up of 12.6 years, 750 women died (130 breast cancer deaths). Compared to stable consumption, the association between cessation and ACM varied by change interval: pre-diagnosis (HR:0.91, CI:0.69-1.21), pre- to post-diagnosis: (HR:1.39, CI:1.12-1.73), post-diagnosis: (HR:0.98, CI:0.70-1.35). Alcohol reduction was not associated with ACM. Among women consuming ≥ 1 drink/day pre-diagnosis, increasing consumption elevated ACM risk (HR:1.83, 95%CI:1.02-3.31). Alcohol reduction or cessation was not associated with a decrease in ACM among older breast cancer survivors. Among those drinking ≥ 1 drink/day, an increase in consumption pre-diagnosis was associated with higher mortality. Findings may be limited by uncontrolled confounding, a low prevalence of heavy drinking, or an insufficient duration of sustained change.

papers.abstract: Patients with high-grade glioma reach surgery during the initial, index hospitalization (urgent), or through scheduled/outpatient pathways. There is a paucity of literature examining what patients require expedited versus elective surgery. This single-center retrospective study describes complications, utilization, and survival by pathway. Adults with WHO grade 3-4 gliomas undergoing primary resection (2021-2026) were classified as urgent (admitted without a planned resection date) or scheduled (discharged and readmitted for planned surgery, or managed exclusively as an outpatient). Primary outcomes were 30-day complications and days alive at home within 30 days of admission for resection (DAH-30). Secondary outcomes were progression free and overall survival. Survival was analyzed with propensity-score overlap weighting and Cox regression. Of 166 patients, 122 underwent urgent resection and 44 scheduled resections; 40 of 44 (91%) proceeded as planned. Urgent patients more often had midline shift (62% vs. 32%), less often seizure (15% vs. 39%), and lower Karnofsky scores (70 vs. 80); all p ≤ 0.002. They had longer index hospitalizations (median 8 vs. 3 days, p < 0.001) and fewer days at home (median 15 vs. 27; adjusted difference - 8.9 days, 95% CI - 12.9 to - 4.8). Complication rates (36% vs. 30%; adjusted OR 1.15, 95% CI 0.52-2.62) and overall survival (median 15.4 vs. 19.0 months, p = 0.758) did not differ detectably. Scheduled resection identified a distinct population, recognizable at initial evaluation by preserved performance status and the absence of midline shift. These patients spent more days at home and required shorter hospitalizations; no harm signal was observed. These data suggest that a substantial proportion of patients with newly diagnosed presumed high grade gliomas can be managed effectively in an expedited, outpatient basis.

papers.abstract: Our purpose was to compare the safety and toxicity profiles of concurrent versus sequential administration of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) and postoperative radiotherapy (RT) in patients with Positive regional nodes, operable, hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer (HER2-). We conducted a real-world, multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolling 364 patients with node-positive, operable HR+/HER2- breast cancer who received postoperative radiotherapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibitors between January 2019 and December 2024. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance baseline covariates between the two arms, yielding 87 patients in each matched group. The primary endpoint was permanent CDK4/6i discontinuation, and secondary endpoints included dose reduction, drug substitution, grade ≥3 toxicities, and symptomatic radiation-induced lung injury (sRILI). No significant intergroup differences were observed in CDK4/6i discontinuation rates before or after PSM (unmatched: 10.4% vs. 8.4%, P=0.536; PSM-matched: 10.3% vs. 9.2%, P=0.798). Similar non-significant findings were identified for dose reduction and drug substitution across unmatched and matched cohorts. For severe toxicities, univariate analysis of the unmatched cohort revealed a significantly higher rate of grade ≥3 drug eruption in the concurrent arm (4.3% vs. 0.4%, unadjusted P=0.013), while this association attenuated to borderline statistical significance after covariate balancing via PSM (4.6% vs. 0.0%, unadjusted P=0.059). No significant between-group differences were detected in sRILI, interstitial pneumonia, grade ≥3 radiation dermatitis, grade ≥3 diarrhea, or hematologic toxicities pre- and post-matching. All grade ≥3 drug eruptions occurred outside radiation fields and presented as diffuse maculopapular rashes involving the trunk and extremities, consistent with CDK4/6i-related hypersensitivity. Concurrent CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and postoperative RT demonstrate a manageable safety and tolerance profile. Given that treatment discontinuation due to ≥G 3 toxicities was observed in both groups, close toxicity monitoring and comprehensive management throughout the treatment course should be implemented when combining RT with CDK4/6i.

papers.abstract: Craniospinal irradiation (CSI) is used for leptomeningeal carcinomatosis (LMC), yet comparative data between proton CSI (pCSI) and photon volumetric modulated arc therapy CSI (xCSI) are limited. We evaluated clinical outcomes and longitudinal toxicity profiles following pCSI versus xCSI in patients with solid tumor LMC. We retrospectively identified adults with solid tumor LMC treated with CSI at a single institution from 2020 to 2025. Toxicities were graded per CTCAE v5.0 at baseline, during treatment, and at 1, 3, and 6 months post-CSI. Overall survival (OS) and central nervous system progression-free survival (CNS-PFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods; Cox models evaluated OS associations. 45 patients initiated CSI (18 xCSI, 27 pCSI). Grade ≥ 3 lymphopenia during treatment was similar (75% xCSI versus 56% pCSI; p = 0.43), whereas Grade ≥ 3 thrombocytopenia occurred only with xCSI (29% versus 0%; p = 0.04). At 3 months, Grade ≥ 3 lymphopenia was higher with pCSI (79% versus 17%; p = 0.02). Non-hematologic Grade ≥ 3 toxicities were rare. OS did not significantly differ (median 8.5 months pCSI versus 4.8 months xCSI; p = 0.50), nor did CNS-PFS (5.9 versus 3.0 months; p = 0.20). On multivariable analysis, worse OS was associated with higher extracranial tumor burden (HR 2.77, 95% CI, 1.20-6.40) and performance status (HR 2.88, 95% CI, 1.01-8.23), but not modality. No statistically significant modality differences in OS or CNS-PFS were detected; baseline performance status and extracranial burden were associated with OS. VMAT-based CSI represents a practical alternative in settings without protons, with careful monitoring of acute hematologic toxicity.

papers.abstract: NF1-associated high-grade gliomas (HGGs) are rare, biologically heterogeneous tumors with poor outcomes. Although MEK inhibitors (MEKis) are established options for selected NF1-associated low-grade gliomas, their role in NF1-associated HGG remains undefined. We describe clinical and radiographic outcomes with MEKis, including mirdametinib. We retrospectively reviewed adult patients with NF1-associated HGG treated at The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center who initiated selumetinib, mirdametinib, or dabrafenib plus trametinib from December 1, 2019, to January 31, 2026. Outcomes included radiographic response and Kaplan-Meier estimates of progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) from MEKi initiation. Progression was defined as the earliest documented radiographic or clinical evidence of progression. Nine patients were included. Median age at HGG onset was 34 years (range, 22-58), and median Karnofsky Performance Status at MEKi initiation was 60 (range, 50-90). Diagnoses were high-grade astrocytoma with piloid features (n = 6), IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (n = 2), and IDH-wildtype HGG/not otherwise specified (n = 1). Most patients received MEKi after prior local and/or systemic therapy. Among three patients treated with mirdametinib, two evaluable patients achieved partial response by Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology criteria. Six patients received selumetinib for 1-7 cycles, and one patient received dabrafenib/trametinib for 2 cycles. Stable disease was the best response among the remaining evaluable patients. Median PFS and OS from MEKi initiation were 2.9 and 9.4 months, respectively. Radiographic partial responses were observed in two patients with NF1-associated HGG treated with mirdametinib, but durability of benefit was limited. The best response with selumetinib and dabrafenib/trametinib was stable disease in evaluable patients. Larger prospective studies are needed to define the role of MEK inhibition in this population.

papers.abstract: Serine metabolism is of growing biologic and therapeutic interest in cancer. Upregulation of the serine synthesis pathway (SSP) can fuel tumor growth, and cancers with this phenotype are often sensitive to. SSP inhibitors. In parallel, dietary restriction of serine and glycine (SG) can suppress some cancers, but the determinants of sensitivity to. this approach are poorly understood. This is especially true in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), where serine metabolism has been less explored. We report that a subset of human AML cell lines and primary samples are completely dependent on external serine, known as serine auxotrophy. These leukemias consistently suppressed the SSP enzyme PSAT1, failed to. synthesize serine, responded to. SG restriction in vivo, and were rescued by restoring PSAT1. We also found that SG restriction synergized with venetoclax in serine auxotrophic AML, and that MECOM rearrangement was strongly associated with PSAT1 suppression and serine auxotrophy. These findings define a metabolically distinct AML subtype and nominate it for targeting by SG restriction.

papers.abstract: Inguinal lymph node dissection (ILND) remains a cornerstone of nodal management in penile cancer, providing definitive treatment for clinically node-positive disease and surgical staging for high-risk clinically node-negative patients when dynamic sentinel node biopsy (DSNB) is unavailable. Despite its oncological importance, ILND is associated with substantial morbidity. Over the past decade, minimally invasive (MI) approaches have emerged as alternatives to open ILND, with the potential to reduce wound-related complications while maintaining oncological efficacy. This Surgery in Motion article provides a practical overview of contemporary open, video-endoscopic (VEIL), and robot-assisted (RAVEIL) ILND techniques, integrating anatomical principles, technical variations, and current clinical evidence. Open ILND remains the reference approach, particularly in patients with advanced nodal disease, while MI techniques may be considered in selected patients with limited nodal disease at experienced centres. Across all approaches, meticulous adherence to anatomical templates, appropriate patient selection, and preservation of lymphatic and vascular structures where oncologically feasible are key principles for minimising morbidity. Emerging robotic and image-guided technologies may further refine ILND, although their clinical benefits and long-term oncological outcomes require further evaluation. This stepwise educational review and accompanying surgical video aim to support surgical training, standardisation, and safe implementation of contemporary ILND techniques.

papers.abstract: Active surveillance (AS) is a recommended option for favorable-risk Gleason grade group 2 (GG2) prostate cancer (PCa), but uptake varies. To describe the nature of progression of confirmed GG2 disease in a well-annotated AS cohort. Participants at the University of California, San Francisco, were diagnosed with cT1-2N0/xM0/x, prostate-specific antigen (PSA) <20 ng/ml, core positivity ≤50%, and GG2 PCa without expansile cribriform or intraductal carcinoma (EC/IDC) at diagnosis, with two or more biopsies on AS from 2000 to 2025. Active surveillance. Outcomes were upgrade (GG3 or higher), volume increase to >50%, EC/IDC, disease progression (upgrade, volume increase, or EC/IDC), active treatment, recurrence (biochemical recurrence or salvage treatment) after radical prostatectomy (RP), metastasis, and PCa-specific mortality (PCSM). Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to identify risk factors for AS outcomes. A total of 329 men were included. At 5 and 10 yr of follow-up, respectively, the upgrade rate was 31% and 58%, volume increase rate was 22% and 31%, EC/IDC development rate was 10% and 41%, disease progression rate was 44% and 79%, active treatment rate was 46% and 65%, and metastasis rate was 0.80% and 3.3%. The 5-yr post-RP recurrence rate was 32%. No PCSM events were recorded within 10 yr. PSA density (PSAD) and positive baseline multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI; Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System 4-5) were associated with disease progression and active treatment. Limitations include the single-institution cohort, a largely Caucasian population, and incomplete mpMRI and genomic testing. Men with confirmed favorable-risk GG2 PCa on AS have moderate rates of disease progression requiring treatment at 10 yr. Metastasis and PCSM rates were low, but confidence intervals are wide and require external validation. Positive mpMRI and increased PSAD were associated with disease progression and can help tailor AS intensity.

papers.abstract: There are substantial regional differences in prostate cancer (PCa) epidemiology reflecting differences in risk factors, screening, management, and access to care. To assess geographical differences and temporal trends in PCa incidence and mortality and PCa risk factors. Estimated incidence and mortality data for the year 2024 and projections to 2050 based on the assumption that 2024 age-specific incidence and mortality rates remain unchanged (not accounting for changes in risk factors and/or treatments) in 185 countries were derived from the International Agency for Research on Cancer's GLOBOCAN 2024 database. A narrative review of the literature summarized risk factors and preventive measures. Worldwide, 1.55 million new PCa cases were estimated in 2024, with an age-standardized rate (ASR) for incidence of 29 per 100 000. Northern America had the highest all-age incidence ASR (81), and South-Central Asia the lowest (7.2). PCa caused an estimated 420 000 deaths (7.5 per 100 000), with the highest mortality ASRs in the Caribbean (29) and the lowest in South-Central Asia (3.4). By 2050, new cases are projected to be 2.88 million (+86%) and deaths 924 000 (+120%), with the largest relative increases in Africa (+156%). Prostate-specific antigen-based screening influences both incidence and geographic variation. Family history, germ line pathogenic variants, polygenic risk scores, and ancestry are risk factors. Disparities in men of African versus European ancestry reflect both tumor biology and unequal access to care, with mortality gaps narrowing in equal-access health systems. No single nutrient or supplement has been shown to reduce PCa incidence. Cigarette smoking and obesity are associated with PCa-specific mortality, whereas physical activity and plant-based or Mediterranean dietary patterns are associated with a lower risk of disease progression. The global burden of PCa because of population increase and aging is projected to rise substantially by 2050, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. Family history, germ line pathogenic variants, and ancestry are risk factors for PCa. Evidence remains insufficient to support any specific preventive intervention, although smoking, diet, and physical activity may modify risk of progression or mortality.

papers.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a major malignant tumor threatening men's global health. The plasticizer acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC), widely used as a substitute for phthalates, is increasingly detected in human tissues; however, its role in PCa cell migration and invasion and the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. This study integrated network toxicology, scRNA-seq, transcriptomic analysis, Mendelian randomization (MR), and machine learning. In vitro, LNCaP cell proliferation, migration, and invasion were evaluated after ATBC treatment. ATBC toxicity targets were predicted using public databases. scRNA-seq data were analyzed to identify key cell clusters and candidate genes. Causal relationships between candidate genes and PCa were assessed by MR, and key genes were validated through multiple cohorts and HPA-based immunohistochemistry data. Molecular docking and virtual gene knockout were employed to explore binding affinity and functional impact. In this study, in-vitro experiments were first performed, and it was found that the proliferation, migration and invasion abilities of ATBC-treated LNCaP cells were significantly altered. Subsequently, scRNA-seq data were analyzed to identify key cells (epithelial cells). Next, public databases were used to predict the toxic targets of ATBC, and the results of scRNA-seq and transcriptomic analyses were integrated to screen for potential target genes of ATBC in PCa. Finally, MR and machine-learning techniques were adopted to obtain the key genes (LPCAT1 and PDK1). In addition, molecular docking results for ATBC confirmed favorable binding affinity between the key genes and ATBC. Virtual knockout results also indicated that the key genes played a role in tumor migration and invasion. ATBC exposure may promote PCa migration and invasion by targeting LPCAT1 and PDK1, thereby perturbing cytoskeletal dynamics and metabolic pathways. These findings offer novel mechanistic insights into microplastic-associated PCa progression.

papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are among the most abundant cells in the tumor microenvironment (TME), with M1 and M2 polarization exhibiting anti-tumorigenic and tumorigenic functions, respectively. Originating from both embryonic precursors and circulating monocytes derived from hematopoietic stem cells, TAMs acquire distinct transcriptional, metabolic, and functional identities shaped by the TME. The interactions in the TME among various cells, including cancerous and non-cancerous cells, can determine the polarization and function of TAMs within the tumor. More recently, TAMs have garnered significant interest as a promising therapeutic target in oncology. The TAMs have been shown to enhance proliferation, metastasis, and angiogenesis in human cancers. Notably, cytokines and chemokines, among others, can regulate the infiltration of TAMs in TME. Given the crucial role of macrophages in regulating inflammation and immune responses, targeting these cells has become a significant focus in cancer immunotherapy. Currently, macrophages have been targeted through three strategies, including suppressing macrophage/monocyte recruitment, depletion of TAMs, and re-education of TAMs. Each of these approaches is being investigated in preclinical models and clinical trials, either as monotherapy or in combination with immune checkpoint inhibitors. TAMs can also be engineered to act as drug delivery tools, carrying nanoparticles directly into tumors. In the clinic, some types of TAMs, marked by proteins like CD163 and CD204, can help predict patient outcomes in several cancers. This review investigates the origins of TAMs and the mechanisms underlying their polarization and metabolism. Furthermore, we study macrophage-driven tumor progression and devising effective targeting strategies, as well as challenges that remain and where the field may go next in macrophage-based cancer treatment. Going forward, combining single-cell profiling with multi-target therapies may offer the best path toward more effective, TAM-based cancer treatments.

papers.abstract: Tobacco smoking is prevalent among patients with rectal cancer, yet its effect on pathologic response to total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) remains unknown. This study evaluated the association between smoking status and pathologic response to TNT in locally advanced rectal cancer, using the neoadjuvant rectal (NAR) score and pathologic complete response (pCR) rate. This retrospective cohort study used the National Cancer Database to identify adults diagnosed in 2023 with clinical stage Ⅱ-Ⅲ rectal adenocarcinoma who received TNT followed by proctectomy. Smoking status at diagnosis was categorized as never, current, or former. Primary outcomes were favorable NAR score (< 8) and pCR (ypT0N0). Among 1767 patients, 49.7% were never smokers, 30.5% former, and 19.8% current smokers. Rates of favorable NAR score and pCR were highest among never smokers (33.4 and 21.7%), intermediate among former smokers (28.8 and 19.9%), and lowest among current smokers (25.5 and 16.3%). On multivariable analysis, current smoking was associated with lower odds of favorable NAR score than was never smoking (odds ratio 0.59; 95% confidence interval 0.40-0.86). A similar trend was seen for pCR, though this did not reach statistical significance (odds ratio 0.58; 95% confidence interval 0.34-1.00). Former smoking was not significantly different from never smoking in terms of a favorable NAR score or pCR. Current smoking status was independently associated with lower rates of response to TNT in locally advanced rectal cancer, whereas former smoking was not when compared with never smoking. These findings identify active tobacco exposure as a potential modifiable risk factor.

papers.abstract: Mast cells (MCs) display phenotypic heterogeneity across tissues and disease contexts, yet their relevance in melanoma remains unclear. Here, we investigated MC phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression using high-dimensional phenotyping of MCs co-cultured with melanoma spheroids, trajectory inference, and transcriptomic analyzes. Human melanoma tissues showed differences in MC phenotypic composition despite comparable abundance between outcome groups, with metastatic melanomas enriched for Tryptase⁺ Chymase- MCs. Melanoma exposure induced MC phenotypic remodeling, characterized by loss of lineage- and effector-associated features and increased PD-1 expression, with more pronounced changes following metastatic melanoma co-culture. Trajectory analysis was consistent with a continuum toward a PD-1⁺ Chymase- phenotype, which was detected in melanoma tissues and enriched within intratumoral regions of metastatic melanomas. Experimentally defined protein changes were used to derive two MC-associated transcriptomic signatures with opposing clinical associations, reflecting lineage- and effector-enriched versus melanoma-remodeled programs. The MC-LE signature was associated with favorable survival and interferon-responsive pathways, whereas the MC-MR signature was associated with poorer survival and tumor-associated pathways. These transcriptomic associations extended beyond melanoma across multiple TCGA cancer cohorts, and independent analysis of MCs from healthy skin, basal cell carcinoma, and melanoma showed corresponding differences in MC-LE-related features. Together, these findings support distinct mast cell phenotypic programs associated with melanoma progression and identify a PD-1⁺ Chymase- MC phenotype enriched in metastatic disease and linked to transcriptomic features of poor survival.

papers.abstract: To describe the current landscape of hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to treat surgical menopause following bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (BSO) in individuals with hereditary ovarian cancer risk in British Columbia, Canada. We aimed to describe current use of HRT, identify factors associated with HRT use and identify potential barriers for uptake and access. Individuals with germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in an ovarian cancer susceptibility gene were identified through the BC Cancer Hereditary Cancer Program (HCP) Progeny database. A cross-sectional survey was administered to collect participant demographics, personal and family cancer history, and participant experiences with HRT. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the sample and logistic regression used to explore associations between sociodemographic variables and reported HRT use. Open text fields were analyzed using inductive quantitative content analysis. In total, 374 responses were received from 1284 potential participants (29.1% response rate). Of participants who have had a BSO, 41% (101/245) report HRT use. In open-text responses, 22% of participants reported lack of support by healthcare professionals and 26% described gaps in counselling about HRT and surgical menopause. In the regression analysis, HRT use was less likely in individuals who: were of increasing age, reported a history of any cancer type and who reported receiving no counselling about HRT (all p < 0.0011 after Bonferroni correction). Barriers to HRT access and uptake exist for individuals at increased risk of ovarian cancer. Together this data indicates that patients require additional support in this area particularly as it relates to education and resources.

papers.abstract: The antiangiogenic pathway is an effective target for recurrent uterine cervical carcinoma (rCC). This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of cabozantinib monotherapy for rCC. This open-label phase II study (NCT04205799) enrolled patients with rCC who previously received platinum-based chemotherapy. Patients received oral cabozantinib (60 mg daily) until progression or discontinuation from any cause. The main objective was based on joint primary endpoint of efficacy (3-month disease control rate, DCR3) and safety (proportion of patients with grade ≥ 2 (CTCAE v5.0) gastro-intestinal (GI) perforation, GI-vaginal and/or genito-urinary (GU) fistula events) according to a Bryant-and-Day design. Key secondary endpoints were progression-free survival (PFS), duration of response (DOR) and safety. Among 57 patients enrolled, 54 received cabozantinib: median age was 55.5 years, 18 patients (33.3%) had received more than two prior lines of treatment; 28 patients (51.9%) had been previously treated with bevacizumab. Median duration of follow-up was 8.9 months. DCR3 was 46.3% [95% CI, 32.8-60.3]. Fistula/perforation occurred in 5 (9.3%) patients. Objective response rate was 9.3%, with a median DOR of 2.5 months. Median PFS was 2.8 months (95% CI, 2.5-4.6). Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 51.9% of patients, most commonly asthenia (15%), hypertension (9%) and mucositis (6%). Dose reductions and treatment interruptions were reported in 26 (48%) and 24 (44%) patients, respectively. Cabozantinib demonstrates efficacy comparable to other anti-angiogenic monotherapy in rCC; however, modest benefit and toxicity do not support further monotherapy development.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Timely and comprehensive molecular classification is essential for therapeutic decision-making in pediatric oncology, yet current diagnostic workflows rely on multi-step, time- and resource-intensive testing strategies. We present a standardized whole-genome sequencing approach with adaptive sampling (AS-WGS) using Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) optimized for pediatric cancers, that enables rapid and comprehensive molecular profiling in a single assay. Methods We designed an AS-WGS panel comprising 380 clinically relevant loci that we applied to the sequencing of 36 pediatric cancer and control samples. To support real-time interpretation, we developed an open-source bioinformatic pipeline (nf-core-oncoseq) enabling on-the-fly analysis during sequencing. We compared the AS-WGS results to those obtained by standard clinical assays, including exome and transcriptome sequencing. Results AS-WGS achieved somatic-grade coverage (mean 172X) in target regions while maintaining pan-genomic coverage (18X), thus supporting genome-wide copy number and methylation analyses. AS-WGS reliably detected all classes of clinically actionable alterations including fusion genes (20/20), small variants (SNVs and indels, in 58/59 mutated genes) and large CNVs (20/21). SNVs were robustly captured down to a 5% allelic frequency, similar to clinical exome sequencing. The PCR-free workflow supported methylation-based tumor classification, providing orthogonal confirmation of hematological and solid tumor subtypes in 9/11 acute lymphoblastic leukemias and in 8/12 solid tumors. All clonal alterations were identified with >5 supporting reads from data generated in the first 24 hours of sequencing (20/20 fusions and 47/47 SNVs with allelic frequencies > 25%), with some, such as large CNVs and methylation predictions, detected within the first hour. Conclusions Our results show that applying AS-WGS to pediatric hematological and solid tumors supports the rapid identification of all classes of genomic alterations and enables methylation-based classification in a single assay. Future efforts aimed at clinical translation will establish its position within the current multi-assay diagnostic landscape.

papers.abstract: Head and neck cancer (HNC) imposes a substantial burden in Aotearoa New Zealand (AoNZ), yet contemporary population-level data on incidence and early mortality across sociodemographic groups remain limited. This population-based retrospective cohort study used New Zealand Cancer Registry to identify all primary HNC diagnoses from 2009 to 2020 (n = 6980). The cases were classified according to ICD-10 subsites. Incidence rates (IRs), age-standardised IRs, and age-standardised rate ratios were estimated by age, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic deprivation, and rurality. Regression models were used to estimate annual percentage change in IRs and to estimate adjusted risk ratios for two-year all-cause mortality. In total 6980 people were diagnosed with HNC; an overall incidence rate of 13.5 per 100,000 person-years (PY). Oropharyngeal cancer (OPC), the most common subsite, increased from 3.4 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2011-4.9 per 100,000 PY in 2018-2020, whereas IRs for oral cavity cancer (OCC), the second most common, were more stable. HNC IRs were higher among males, older adults, Māori, Pacific Peoples and people living in the most socioeconomically deprived areas, with subsite-specific differences: Māori experienced higher OPC incidence rates, while Pacific Peoples experienced higher OCC IRs. Within two years of diagnosis, 25.2% of patients had died. Two-year all-cause mortality was 44.4% for hypopharyngeal cancer, 30.9% for OCC, and 22.7% for OPC. Among people diagnosed with HNC, after adjusting for available sociodemographic factors and treatment timing, two-year all-cause mortality was higher for Māori, Pacific Peoples, and those in the most deprived quintile. Rurality showed no consistent association with incidence or two-year mortality. These findings indicate an OPC-driven shift in HNC epidemiology in AoNZ and a persistent inequitable burden of both disease occurrence and early mortality, supporting stronger surveillance and equity-focused cancer-control responses.

papers.abstract: Main duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (MD-IPMN) carries a substantial risk of malignant transformation and often requires surgical resection.1,2 Preservation of the remnant pancreas remains an important goal, particularly in elderly patients.3,4 Therefore, determining the optimal extent of resection requires a careful balance between oncological safety and preservation of pancreatic function.5,6 The utility of intraoperative pancreatoscopy during robotic pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) for this purpose has not been well established.7 METHODS: We present two elderly patients with MD-IPMN who underwent RPD combined with intraoperative pancreatoscopy. After pancreatic transection, a Spyglass was introduced through a robotic port #1 and advanced into the remnant pancreatic duct under robotic guidance. The main pancreatic duct and branch ducts were systematically inspected for findings suspicious for high-grade dysplasia or skip lesions.8 Frozen-section analysis of the pancreatic margin was performed in both cases. The patients were in their 70s with pancreatic head IPMN and pancreatic duct dilation. Intraoperative pancreatoscopy demonstrated no suspicious lesions within the remnant pancreas. Frozen-section analysis confirmed the absence of carcinoma or high-grade dysplasia at the pancreatic margin. Based on these findings, no additional pancreatic resection was required, and the remnant pancreas was preserved in both patients. Final pathology revealed mixed-type IPMN with high-grade dysplasia and no invasive carcinoma in both cases. Intraoperative pancreatoscopy can be safely integrated into RPD and serves as an adjunct to preoperative imaging, potentially facilitating targeted biopsy. This approach may support preservation of the remnant pancreas in elderly patients with MD-IPMN.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by severe immunosuppression and metabolic reprogramming, yet the spatial dynamics of lipid flux between malignant and stromal cells remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a profound, type-specific metabolic rewiring in HCC driven by the widespread downregulation of fatty acid transport protein 5 (FATP5). FATP5 deficiency in malignant cells selectively attenuates the uptake of long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs), creating an extracellular lipid surplus that is passively sequestered by neighboring FATP3-expressing tumor-associated endothelial cells (TECs). Within TECs, accumulated LCFAs function as endogenous ligands that activate the nuclear receptor PPARγ, culminating in the robust transcriptional upregulation and paracrine secretion of the chemokine CXCL12. Endothelial-derived CXCL12 subsequently engages CXCR4 on infiltrating CD8+ T cells, inducing PD-1 expression and driving terminal T-cell exhaustion, thereby establishing an immunosuppressive niche that accelerates tumor progression. Importantly, our data suggest that HCC subtypes marked by FATP5 depletion and CXCL12+ TEC enrichment may possess potential therapeutic susceptibility to PPARγ antagonism or anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade. Besides affecting the secretory function of TECs, accumulated LCFAs can impair endothelial barrier function, thereby creating a microenvironment with hematogenous metastasis risk. Collectively, our findings delineate a novel tumor-promoting microenvironment cascade orchestrated by LCFA spatial redistribution, providing a promising mechanistic foundation to support the future development of targeted precision interventions for FATP5-low HCC.

papers.abstract: Advanced sarcomas remain therapeutically challenging. We evaluated treatment implementation and clinical outcomes after molecular tumor board recommendations. We retrospectively analyzed 125 sarcoma patients discussed in our multidisciplinary Molecular and Familial Tumor Board between 2017 and 2023. Clinical benefit was assessed by treatment implementation and by the ratio of progression-free survival on molecularly guided therapy versus the preceding treatment line (PFS2/PFS1). Overall survival (OS) was measured from first board discussion. A total of 252 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant records across 133 genes were identified. Molecular profiling enabled therapy recommendations in 71 of 125 patients (56.8%), with treatment implementation in 41 (32.8%). PFS2/PFS1 evaluation was feasible in 29 patients, and nine (31.0%) had a documented ratio > 1.3. Median PFS2 was 102 days (95% CI 63-233). Two of seven patients (28.6%) receiving poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitor-containing regimens had ratios > 1.3. Median OS in 124 patients was 14.6 months (95% CI 11.7-18.5; global log-rank p = 0.220). Molecular tumor board-guided therapy identified treatment options for selected sarcoma patients. Prolonged disease control in individual PARP-treated cases provides a positive signal that warrants prospective evaluation.

papers.abstract: A recent population-based cohort study of Seoul residents in South Korea reported increased incidence of several cancers within one year of SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We examined whether a short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends was detectable at the national vaccination rollout, using a design that does not compare vaccinated with unvaccinated individuals. We conducted an interrupted time series analysis of Korea National Health Insurance Service data for 36,024,394 individuals born between 1955 and 2004, covering February 2011 to September 2025 (176 months). The intervention point was August 2021, when cumulative first-dose coverage exceeded 50%. Monthly incidence of 13 cancer categories defined by ICD-10 code ranges and of four site-specific cancers (stomach, colorectum, lung and prostate) was compared with counterfactual forecasts from ARIMA/SARIMA models, and segmented regression estimated immediate level and trend changes (significance threshold P < 0.01). The placement of the intervention point was varied from 0 to 18 months, and the resulting estimates were compared with those obtained at 30 placebo points in the pre-pandemic period. Overall, 89.3% of the population received at least one dose. No immediate level change (relative risk 0.923-1.072) or trend change (0.995-1.005) reached significance for any of the 13 categories, and none reached significance for the four site-specific cancers. Across the lag grid, 2.0% of estimates met the threshold, compared with 4.1% at placebo points. The 99% confidence limits excluded immediate increases larger than 8.9% to 23.0% across the 13 categories and 8.1% to 23.4% across the four site-specific cancers. The national SARS-CoV-2 vaccination rollout in South Korea was not accompanied by a detectable short-term, population-level change in cancer incidence trends over the 50 months that followed. papers.abstract: We examined the associations of parity and breastfeeding with postmenopausal breast density, longitudinal changes in breast density, and breast cancer risk, and assessed the extent to which breast density mediates these relationships. We analyzed a cohort of women who underwent mammography in 2009-2010 and had at least one follow-up mammogram through 2016. Parity and breastfeeding history were self-reported, breast density was classified using Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS), and relative risks (RRs) were estimated using Poisson regression. Mediation analysis evaluated the contributions of baseline breast density and its longitudinal change. Lower parity and shorter breastfeeding duration were associated with higher baseline breast density and less favorable density trajectories over time, including a greater likelihood of increasing density and a lower likelihood of decreasing density. Compared with women with at least two children who breastfed for > 12 months, women with one child who did not breastfeed had a higher breast cancer risk (RR: 1.53; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.43-1.64), with a clear dose-response pattern across parity and breastfeeding categories. Parity showed stronger associations than breastfeeding duration with both breast density and breast cancer risk, and these associations were generally stronger among women aged 65 years or older. Baseline breast density and its longitudinal change mediated approximately 10%-15% of the associations between reproductive factors and breast cancer risk. These findings suggest that reproductive history has long-term effects on breast tissue composition and partly explains subsequent breast cancer risk in postmenopausal women.

papers.abstract: Fifty years ago, Zech et al. in this journal described for the first time the t(8;14) as a recurrent chromosomal aberration in Burkitt lymphoma (BL). Nevertheless, in regions where BL is not endemic, a subset of lymphomas with features of BL lacks the t(8;14)/IG::MYC and instead represents high-grade B-cell lymphoma with 11q aberration (HGBCL,11q). As Zech et al. already noted the cell line BJAB to be an exception as BL from a 5-year Kenyan girl in being EBV-negative, lacking the t(8;14) but showing a chromosome 11 aberration, we here revisited and updated the molecular features of BJAB. Genetic analyses confirmed its East African origin and absence of IG::MYC but unraveled complex 11q aberrations, including gains in 11q14.1-q23.1, loss of 11q23.2qter, and, notably, a nonreciprocal 5'KMT2A::CLTC3'-fusion. The mutational landscape contained genes typically mutated in mature B-cell lymphomas but no driver genes restricted to BL. Therefore, we hypothesize that BJAB derives from an African HGBCL,11q. To investigate the presence of this entity in East Africa, we analyzed 24 cases with Burkitt or high-grade morphology diagnosed at Kenyatta National Hospital. Twenty cases fulfilled the morphological and immunophenotypical criteria for the diagnosis of BLs (11 EBV-positive, 9 EBV-negative). Genetic testing in these cases identified one EBV-negative case (20 years) as MYC-nonrearranged but displaying the typical 11q pattern, thus representing HGBCL,11q. Among the four HGBCL with intermediate features, two showed gains in 11q including the region typically deleted in HGBCL,11q. Our findings establish HGBCL,11q as a relevant differential molecular diagnosis to Burkitt lymphoma in sub-Saharan Africa.

papers.abstract: Seminal extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold promise as a source of biomarkers for urogenital cancers. In this study, small seminal EVs were isolated from healthy donors by size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) and three ultracentrifugation (UC) protocols, with or without filtration. EV samples prepared by UC had a higher abundance of typical EV-related molecules such as CD9, CD81, and Alix, compared to SEC preparations. However, ribosomal and ER-related proteins were more enriched in SEC samples. Furthermore, the level of several nonvesicular proteins and/or EV-corona proteins was higher in SEC samples. The addition of a filtration step in the UC protocols also reduced the abundance of these proteins. Finally, we found that the isolation protocol affected the presence of prostate cancer-specific proteins in the EV samples, with membrane proteins such as FOLH1, TMPRSS2, and PSCA enriched in samples prepared by UC. In conclusion, our results suggest that SEC and UC enrich for different EV populations, which should be considered when analyzing cancer biomarkers. Moreover, UC samples contained fewer nonvesicular proteins and/or EV-corona proteins, which may enable a more precise detection of EV-based cancer biomarkers.

papers.abstract: Gynaecological malignancies account for over 1.4 million new diagnoses, with outcomes constrained by late-stage presentation and chemoresistance. Dysregulated redox homeostasis is a hallmark of tumourigenesis. Tumour cells maintain elevated basal reactive oxygen species (ROS), which support proliferative signalling but may also increase susceptibility to further oxidative stress. Vitamin D, acting through the vitamin D receptor (VDR), has antiproliferative and pro-apoptotic effects across cancer models, but its ability to amplify ROS beyond an apoptotic threshold in gynaecological malignancies remains unresolved. We conducted a narrative literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE, ClinicalTrials.gov and the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results databases, using terms related to vitamin D and its metabolites, ROS/oxidative stress, apoptosis and gynaecological malignancies. Preclinical evidence indicates that calcitriol and related compounds can induce ROS-mediated mitochondrial apoptosis, modulate autophagy and arrest the cell cycle. In ovarian cancer, non-HGSOC cell data suggest that mutant TP53 may alter calcitriol responses, requiring validation in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma models. In cervical cancer, calcitriol radiosensitises human papillomavirus-positive cell lines through autophagy suppression, whilst an in vivo calcitriol-cisplatin study reported improved survival. In endometrial cancer, thioredoxin-interacting protein induction is a candidate mechanism for selective ROS-mediated apoptosis, although this remains context-dependent. Clinical evidence is heterogeneous: higher 25-hydroxyvitamin D status has shown modest inverse associations with ovarian cancer mortality; small trials report regression or reduced recurrence of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia; no randomised controlled trial evidence supports efficacy in invasive cervical cancer; and associations with endometrial cancer incidence are largely null. Current evidence does not support vitamin D supplementation as an oncology-specific intervention. Future research should prioritise biomarker-stratified trials incorporating VDR genotype, CYP24A1 profiling, pre-specified 25(OH)D targets and pharmacokinetically informed dosing.

papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is often limited by tumor-intrinsic DNA repair and an immunosuppressive microenvironment, both of which are reinforced by lactate accumulation. Here, we develop a CXCR4-engineered enucleated hepatocyte cytoplast platform decorated with Au-Pt Janus nanorobots (AP/LCCXCR4) to deplete intratumoral lactate and amplify radiation-induced oxidative stress. The hepatocyte cytoplasts home to tumors and consume lactate through gluconeogenesis, reducing repair-associated protein lactylation and impairing MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 (MRN) co-fractionation and chromatin recruitment, thereby impairing double-strand break repair. In parallel, the Au-Pt nanorobots enhance reactive oxygen species generation under acidic tumor conditions, increasing radiation damage. In radioresistant colorectal cancer models and a metastatic cervical cancer model, AP/LCCXCR4 combined with radiotherapy sustains DNA damage, promotes immunogenic cell death, reduces immunosuppressive myeloid and regulatory T (Treg) cell populations, enhances dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell activation, and improves tumor control and survival.

papers.abstract: Inflammatory transcriptional responses mediated by NF-κB are diverse despite similar upstream activation signals. Because phosphorylation of the NF-κB subunit RelA/p65 promotes interaction with co-activators CREB-binding protein/E1A binding protein p300 (CBP/p300) and selectively affects gene expression, we asked whether this modification distinguishes regulatory architectures underlying distinct immune functions. In macrophages carrying a Rela Ser276Ala mutation, p65 phosphorylation at serine 276 (S276) was dispensable for NF-κB binding to primed enhancers but essential for recruitment to nucleosome-occluded regions lacking pre-bound transcription factors (TFs) and activating histone marks. Such latent enhancers required phosphorylated NF-κB to recruit CBP/p300, promote histone acetylation, and open chromatin. Genes linked to these enhancers, including inflammatory mediators, were selectively impaired in S276A macrophages. Although antiviral responses remained intact, Rela Ser276Ala mice resisted endotoxin shock but were susceptible to bacterial infection. Thus, NF-κB responses are functionally partitioned by enhancer architecture: phosphorylation-sensitive sites define a latent enhancer compartment with NF-κB-dominated regulatory architecture, whereas primed sites are embedded in broader networks of lineage-determining and inducible TFs, yielding distinct biological outputs.

papers.abstract: Physical activity promotes health primarily by decelerating the aging process. Bone is one of the tissues capable of sensing mechanical force and can adapt to different physical demands. However, its role in whole-body aging is unknown. We found that reduced mechano-sensing in osteocytes, caused by deletion of the mechanosensory channel, Piezo1, accelerated whole-body aging in mice. Dynamic tibial axial loading (DTAL) in mice at 20-24 months of age extended both healthspan and lifespan (9.4%/79.5 days). Furthermore, DTAL reversed bone marrow immunosenescence and induced anti-aging and protective factors while downregulating pro-aging and pro-inflammatory factors. We also identified pigment epithelium-derived factor (PEDF) as a novel mechano-responsive anti-aging factor that is highly associated with healthy aging in humans. Thus, our findings highlighted an essential role for bone mechano-sensing in whole-body aging. This could potentially be manipulated to prevent aging, extend health, and aid those unable to exercise or with decreased mobility.

papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) and its progression to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remain major unmet clinical challenges for which effective therapies are lacking. Although sensory neurons are recognized as key regulators of tissue injury and repair via neuroimmune crosstalk, their organization and function within the kidney are poorly understood. Here, we delineate a renal neuroimmune axis in which nociceptive neurons protect against ischemia-reperfusion (I/R)-induced kidney injury. Using whole-organ tissue clearing and three-dimensional imaging, we mapped an extensive network of nociceptive sensory fibers throughout the renal parenchyma. Ablation of TRPV1+ nociceptors aggravated renal dysfunction, tubular necrosis, and fibrosis after I/R, whereas chemogenetic activation conferred protection. Mechanistically, the sensory neuropeptide calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), which is upregulated after injury, acts via the CALCRL-RAMP1 receptor complex on monocytes/macrophages, engaging the cAMP-PKA pathway to suppress pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine expression, thereby limiting myeloid infiltration and tubular injury. Importantly, we also found reduced renal CGRP abundance in kidneys from individuals with diabetes and older adults, who are at high risk for AKI and CKD, as well as in corresponding mouse models. In these vulnerable settings, exogenous CGRP more effectively reduced I/R-induced kidney injury. Our findings establish a dorsal root ganglia-kidney neuroimmune circuit that restrains I/R-induced renal inflammation and identify CGRP signaling as a potential therapeutic target to mitigate AKI and its progression to CKD, particularly in high-risk diabetic and elderly populations.

papers.abstract: Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to identify genes involved in complex traits and to infer the direction of gene effects on traits. However, despite their popularity, it remains unclear how accurately TWAS recover the true direction of a gene's effect on a trait. Here we estimate the false sign rate of TWAS for plasma proteins, leveraging the expectation that increased gene expression should generally increase protein expression. We then extend this framework to complex traits, where loss-of-function burden tests provide the expected direction of effect. In both analyses, we observe high discordance with expectations, with TWAS showing a false sign rate of 23% for plasma proteins and 33% for complex traits. We propose that much of the sign discordance arises when expression quantitative trait loci in non-trait-relevant tissues tag haplotypes associated with traits in genome-wide association studies via distinct, tightly linked regulatory variants, yielding spurious TWAS associations with the correct genes but with unreliable direction of effect. These findings show that TWAS-based direction-of-effect estimates should be interpreted with caution and raise concerns about the reliability of TWAS more broadly.

papers.abstract: Wild emmer wheat (Triticum turgidum ssp. dicoccoides, BBAA), the wild progenitor of cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats, provides an important reference for investigating centromere reorganization during polyploidization and domestication. Here we generated a near-complete genome assembly of wild emmer wheat, including centromeric regions for all 14 centromeres. Comparative analyses with cultivated tetraploid and hexaploid wheats revealed extensive variation in centromere-associated sequences and centromere-proximal structure, as well as distinct subgenome-associated patterns in the A and B subgenomes. The A subgenome was characterized by positional shifts and sequence turnover of CRW-rich centromere-derived blocks, whereas the B subgenome showed reduced CentT566 satellite abundance accompanied by localized retention or expansion on specific chromosomes. These results provide a high-resolution tetraploid wheat reference and reveal subgenome-associated patterns of centromere remodeling during wheat polyploid evolution.

papers.abstract: Current vaccine adjuvants, such as aluminum salts and emulsions, are limited by weak induction of cytotoxic T cell immunity and restricted ability to promote T helper type 1 responses, highlighting the need for safer and more effective alternatives. Here we show that microparticles generated from erythrocytes by controlled ultraviolet irradiation function as potent T helper type 1-skewing adjuvants that enhance tumour antigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses in vitro and in multiple mouse tumour models. Following uptake by dendritic cells, these microparticles traffic to lysosomes and deliver haem cargo that is subsequently transported to the nucleus. Mechanistically, the particles elevate lysosomal pH, promoting lysosome movement towards the nucleus and enabling haem transfer, where haem activates REV-ERB⍺ and forms a co-repressor complex that suppresses peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma, thereby relieving inhibition of dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation. In vaccination settings, combining tumour antigens with erythrocyte-derived microparticles enhances cytotoxic T cell activation and suppresses tumour growth with minimal toxicity. These findings establish host-derived vesicles as a promising platform for next-generation cancer vaccine adjuvants.

papers.abstract: Local activation of regulatory T (Treg) cells represents a promising strategy for wound repair and tissue regeneration. However, current Treg-based therapies rely on adoptive cell transfer, which requires ex vivo expansion and reinfusion, posing challenges to donor variability and tissue specificity. Here we engineer a hydrogel-based system for in situ Treg activation at injury sites through the controlled release of AS2863619 (AS), a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor. AS is incorporated into collagen hydrogels at concentrations exceeding its solubility limit, reducing burst release and extending the release half-life. This continuous exposure to Treg-inducing agents stabilizes Foxp3 expression in CD4+ T cells, thereby enabling Treg induction and stabilization. The incorporation of laponite nanoparticles further slows AS release and prolongs drug retention. In a calvarial bone-defect model, AS-loaded hydrogels induce dose-dependent Treg cell activation, reduce pro-inflammatory macrophage responses and enhance bone regeneration. Notably, AS-laponite hydrogels achieve complete defect bridging in some cases. By providing spatiotemporal control over Treg populations without the need for cell isolation and expansion, this approach offers a scalable alternative for immunomodulation and tissue repair.

papers.abstract: Improving outcomes for high-risk acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) patients requires increasingly personalized treatment strategies that leverage molecular and omics-based assays as well as functional screens. However, to date, only a few of these approaches are clinically actionable and easily adopted in clinical settings. To that end, we report a combination drug screening assay (GradientScreen) that correlates with clinical outcomes using standard paediatric ALL treatment protocols. This assay uses a microfluidic device to generate overlapping drug gradients and implements an analysis framework that characterizes drug synergy and efficacy in a ratiometric manner. Using partial least squares regression, we show that our combination response metrics correlate with both minimal residual disease (MRD) following initiation of treatment and later clinical end-points. Here, we further demonstrate that this system could be used to evaluate response to experimental therapeutic regimens in patients who did not respond to standard treatment. This assay can serve as a research-enabling tool for the field, with potential to integrate into clinical pathology workflows to identify difficult-to-treat ALL patients and screen for alternative treatment strategies at diagnosis.

papers.abstract: Cytokines are critical regulators of central nervous system (CNS) integrity, acting not only as immune messengers but also as signals that coordinate interactions among glial and neuronal cells, resident macrophages, such as microglia and border-associated macrophages, and infiltrating leukocytes. These circuits establish basal immune tone, shape responses to perturbation, and promote tissue adaptation and recovery. In this Review, we examine selected cytokine pathways across homeostasis, inflammatory or degenerative tissue damage and repair to develop a framework for how cytokine networks preserve, destabilize and restore CNS integrity. We focus on CSF-1, IL-34, TGFβ and IL-33 in homeostasis; IL-1, TNF, GM-CSF and IFNγ in inflammation; type I and II interferons in antiviral and neurodegenerative states; and IL-12 at the interface of innate sensing, adaptive immunity and tissue-protective adaptation. By focusing on instructive modules, we highlight broader organizing principles and how cytokine miscalibration can lead to neurological disease across diverse contexts.

papers.abstract: DNA's anti-parallel structure presents a topological challenge to the replisome, as leading and lagging strands must be synthesized in opposite directions. How lagging-strand synthesis is coordinated with leading-strand synthesis remains unresolved in eukaryotes. To address this question, we directly visualized the dynamics of lagging-strand polymerases Pol α and Pol δ at active replication forks using single-molecule imaging in Xenopus nuclear extracts. Surprisingly, we find that neither Pol α nor Pol δ is stably tethered to the replisome. Instead, lagging-strand synthesis occurs distributively and entails the rapid recruitment of new molecules of Pol α and Pol δ for each Okazaki fragment. Consequently, leading- and lagging-strand synthesis are not intrinsically coupled. We propose that metazoans solve the problem of anti-parallel replication not by actively coordinating leading- and lagging-strand synthesis, but instead simply by recruiting new polymerases to synthesize each Okazaki fragment.

papers.abstract: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

papers.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity and plasticity are hallmarks of cancer that contribute to tumor growth and therapy resistance. Here, we investigated metabolic heterogeneity in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive cancer type with considerable plasticity between neuroendocrine (NE) and non-NE cellular states. Through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, we identified a universal dependency on exogenous cysteine/cystine (Cys) across all NE/non-NE SCLC cell states. Notably, NE and non-NE cells with low ASCL1 transcription factor levels underwent ferroptosis upon Cys depletion, whereas ASCL1high cells underwent apoptosis while remaining resistant to ferroptosis. This ferroptosis resistance was driven by the direct transcriptional activation of GCH1 by ASCL1, resulting in increased levels of the antioxidants BH4/BH2. Accordingly, combined Cys depletion and inhibition of BH4/BH2 synthesis reduced tumor growth in patient-derived xenografts. These findings demonstrate that metabolic state influences cell-death susceptibility in SCLC and provide a rationale for therapeutic strategies that exploit these metabolic differences.

papers.abstract: Whether a decline in taurine drives aging is debated, and despite high millimolar intracellular concentrations, its function as a potential guardian of cytosolic homeostasis is unclear. Here, we show that aging increases circulating taurine concentrations in humans and mice. Further elevating taurine in aged mice enhances health span, engaging anti-inflammatory pathways previously linked to youthfulness, and reduces mortality from sepsis and inflammasome-mediated inflammation, suggesting an enantiostatic response. Mechanistically, diverse NLRP3-specific "danger signals" induce taurine efflux from macrophages as a proximal step to activate the inflammasome and the resultant pyroptosis. Taurine restoration in macrophages prevents NLRP3-induced trans-Golgi network disassembly, thereby suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Conversely, lowering taurine biosynthesis combined with reduced bioavailability in macrophages exacerbated inflammasome activation. In humans, sustained caloric restriction elevates adipose tissue taurine and is accompanied by lower inflammation. Together, we identify taurine as an immunometabolic rheostat that links danger sensing to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, suggesting taurine-based strategies to alleviate inflammaging and inflammasomopathies.

papers.abstract: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells are critical effectors of anti-tumor immunity. Cytotoxic lymphocytes eliminate tumor cells by releasing perforin (Prf1), a pore-forming protein that enables granzymes (Gzms) to enter target cells and trigger both caspase-dependent and -independent cell death. Here, we uncover a previously unrecognized, Gzm-independent function of Prf1. We find that Prf1 directly induces tumoral ferroptosis, an iron- and lipid-dependent form of cell death. Mechanistically, Prf1-mediated pore formation drives endocytosis of the transferrin receptor, which increases cellular iron uptake. Prf1 promotes the formation of endosomal-mitochondrial contacts, which leads to mitochondrial iron accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and tumor cell ferroptosis. Dietary iron supplementation suppresses tumor progression in murine tumor models in a Prf1-dependent manner. Higher Prf1 expression correlates with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint blockade in patients with cancer. These findings define a Gzm-independent function of Prf1 as a direct executioner of cancer cell death through ferroptosis.

papers.abstract: The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

papers.abstract: Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic 'interphases' may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g-factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2. They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe3GeTe2, producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.

papers.abstract: Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine‑derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state‑of‑the‑art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate‑driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate‑induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.
