papers.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation-based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

papers.abstract: CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in KRAS-driven non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a KRASG12D mouse model, CASTOR1 deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRASG12D inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to KRAS-driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

papers.abstract: Mutations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDHm) define a distinct molecular class of gliomas. IDHm converts α-ketoglutarate (α-KG) to the oncometabolite D-2-hydroxyglutarate (D-2HG), which drives tumorigenesis. The IDHm inhibitor vorasidenib suppresses D-2HG production and prolongs progression-free survival in some, but not all, patients. Here, using patient-derived models, genetically engineered glioma cells, orthotopic xenografts, and patient tissue, we showed that phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) mediates intrinsic resistance to vorasidenib by sustaining D-2HG production despite IDHm inhibition. Silencing PHGDH suppressed residual D-2HG synthesis and restored vorasidenib sensitivity in resistant models, whereas PHGDH overexpression restored D-2HG production and induced resistance in sensitive models. Importantly, restoration of intracellular D-2HG rescued growth despite continued vorasidenib treatment, demonstrating a causal role for residual D-2HG production in the resistant phenotype. Mechanistically, a permissive chromatin state characterized by increased H3K4me3, reduced H3K27me3, and enhanced ATF4 occupancy at the PHGDH promoter facilitated PHGDH upregulation in resistant models. Pharmacologic induction of this chromatin state induced PHGDH expression, restored D-2HG production, and conferred resistance to vorasidenib in sensitive models. Consistently, tumor tissue from patients with poor response to IDHm inhibitor treatment exhibited higher PHGDH expression, coupled with the ATF4-enriched permissive chromatin state observed in resistant models. Finally, deuterium metabolic imaging of D-2HG production from diethyl-[3,3'-2H]-α-KG provided an early, non-invasive readout of response and resistance to vorasidenib in vivo. Collectively, this study identifies a chromatin-regulated ATF4-PHGDH-D-2HG axis as a mechanism of intrinsic resistance to IDHm inhibition and establishes diethyl-[3,3'-2H]-α-KG as a metabolic imaging probe for interrogating treatment response in IDHm gliomas.

papers.abstract: Understanding how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function in tissues requires approaches that link phenotypes to mechanisms across different spatial scales. Here, we present automated multimodal multiplexed microscopy for image cytometry (A.M3.I.CO), a correlative imaging platform that combines multiscale resolution, from millimeters to nanometers, with automated workflows for high-throughput phenotypic profiling and targeted single-molecule analysis in situ. Applying A.M3.I.CO, we observed that 53BP1 is recruited at transcribed p53 target genes independently of the activating stimulus, providing evidence for the formation of a putative complex between 53BP1, p53, and the basal transcription machinery in single cells, as also supported by in vivo observations in tumor models. Extending our measurements to p63 and p73, we found that 53BP1 localized at p63- and p73-targeted transcription sites, suggesting a broader role in participating in p53 family-dependent transcription. These findings indicate an additional genome-surveillance pathway in transcriptional control regulating diverse cellular functions while establishing A.M3.I.CO as a platform for spatially resolved functional analysis.

papers.abstract: The I-SPY2.2 trial tests personalized treatment strategies to improve outcomes while reducing exposure to standard chemotherapy in patients with high-risk early breast cancer (EBC). To evaluate the efficacy and safety of trastuzumab-deruxtecan (T-DXd), an antibody drug conjugate targeting low ERBB2 (formerly HER2) expression, combined with rilvegostomig (R), a bispecific antibody targeting programmed cell death 1 protein and T-cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain as initial therapy in I-SPY2.2 (RT-DXd). This phase 2, multicenter, adaptively randomized neoadjuvant trial enrolled patients with high-risk stage II/III ERBB2-negative EBC (including those with ERBB2 low/ultralow tumors), as stratified by hormone receptor (HR) status and response-predictive subtypes. It was conducted at 30 sites in the US; efficacy data were analyzed continuously during the trial to update probabilities and other analyses before publication. Participants received up to 3 sequential treatment blocks, based on response and subtype: RT-DXd (block A), taxane-based therapy with/without immunotherapy (block B), and doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide (AC) with/without immunotherapy (block C). The primary end point was pathologic complete response (pCR). Safety assessments included adverse events (AEs), with focused monitoring for interstitial lung disease (ILD). A total of 182 individuals (mean [SD] age: RT-DXd, 48.1 [13.1] years; control, 50.9 [12.0] years) participated in the trial. Eighty-eight were randomized to the contemporary control arm, and 108 of 289 remaining participants (37%) were randomized to RT-DXd; 3 participants did not receive block A treatment, and 11 did not receive the assigned control treatment, leaving the intention-to-treat population with 105 and 77 evaluable participants. Among 105 patients treated with RT-DXd in block A, the modeled pCR rate was 54% in immune-positive tumors, which met the predefined threshold for success. Similar pCR rates were observed in HR-positive, immune-positive disease (57%) and HR-negative, immune-positive disease (52%). Across all treatment blocks, overall pCR rates were similar to control regimens; however, among immune-positive patients who experienced pCR, 21 (62%) required only block A, and 33 (97%) avoided anthracycline-based chemotherapy. Enrollment was paused twice to evaluate grade 2 or higher ILD and resumed after data safety monitoring board approval. The most common AEs were fatigue and nausea. Serious AEs included pulmonary embolism and ILD (3 of 105 [2.9%] each). ILD occurred in 13 (12.4%), including 1 grade 3 event, and was identified early with serial chest computed tomography monitoring. This randomized clinical trial found that treatment with RT-DXd demonstrated promising activity, with mostly low-grade toxic effects in immune-positive, ERBB2-negative EBC. Unlike immune-negative patients, many immune-positive patients who experienced pCR avoided standard chemotherapy, including anthracyclines, supporting further evaluation in biomarker-selected populations. papers.abstract: Total shoulder arthroplasty is associated with moderate-to-severe postoperative pain. The aim of this systematic review was to assess the available literature and provide PROSPECT (PROcedure SPECific Postoperative Pain ManagemenT) recommendations for optimal pain management after total shoulder arthroplasty. A systematic review utilising PROSPECT methodology was performed. Randomised controlled trials and systematic reviews published in the English language that assessed postoperative pain using analgesic, anaesthetic and surgical interventions were identified from databases. Of the 1809 articles identified, 30 randomised controlled trials and seven systematic reviews/meta-analyses met our inclusion criteria. Interventions that improved postoperative pain relief included: paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs; dexamethasone; interscalene brachial plexus block and, as an alternative, local infiltration analgesia. Conflicting evidence was found for continuous interscalene brachial plexus block (catheter) or liposomal bupivacaine for interscalene block or local infiltration analgesia. No evidence was found for a specific surgical technique. In the absence of contraindication, the analgesic regimen should include: paracetamol; a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug administered peri-operatively and continued postoperatively; intravenous dexamethasone (8-10 mg); and postoperative opioids for rescue analgesia. As a regional technique, an interscalene brachial plexus block with a single-bolus injection of long-acting local anaesthetic (bupivacaine or ropivacaine), but not liposomal bupivacaine, should be provided. In case of contraindications or absence of expertise, local infiltration analgesia is a reasonable alternative. Further studies are required to investigate the analgesic benefit of a continuous infusion for the interscalene brachial plexus block.

papers.abstract: Gastric mixed neuroendocrine-non-neuroendocrine neoplasms (MiNENs) are aggressive malignancies that exhibit complex cellular heterogeneity driven by the dual lineages. The dismal patient survival rates highlight the need to elucidate the cellular origin of gastric MiNENs and the key regulatory mechanisms to develop improved treatment strategies. Here, we identified a gastric POU2F3+epithelial population as a potential cell of origin for gastric MiNENs. Lineage tracing and single-cell RNA sequencing further identified that POU2F3+ cells include three distinct subpopulations with divergent differentiation trajectories: progenitor cells (SOX2+SOX9+), tuft cells (POU2F3+DCLK1+), and neuroendocrine cells (SYP+CHGA+). Combined Rb1/Trp53 deletion and MYC overexpression in POU2F3+ epithelial cells (Pou2f3-CreERT; Rb1fl/fl; Trp53fl/fl; LSL-MycT58A) led to the rapid development of gastric MiNENs containing both neuroendocrine and non-neuroendocrine lesions, recapitulating human gastric MiNENs pathology. Transcription factor activity analysis and spatial transcriptomics revealed SOX2 and SOX9 as critical regulators driving subpopulation specification, with SOX2 and SOX9 being enriched in dysplasia and adenocarcinoma, respectively. Bulk RNA sequencing further showed increased expression of CXCL5 in gastric MiNENs, and inhibition of CXCL5 reduced the growth of tumor organoids and xenografts in mouse models. Together these findings offer a physiologically relevant model for studying gastric MiNENs and identify CXCL5 as a potential therapeutic target for this heterogeneous cancer.

papers.abstract: Sonidegib, a Hedgehog pathway inhibitor, can induce clinical and imaging remission in locally advanced basal cell carcinoma (BCC). Residual deep tumor may persist after malignant dermoscopic and ultrasound features disappear. This case series assessed the utility and limitations of 20-30 MHz high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) for confirming complete imaging remission after sonidegib. Three patients with nodular BCC received sonidegib 200 mg daily (October 2024-May 2026). Two achieved complete imaging remission, defined as resolution of malignant imaging features with residual non-malignant hypoechoic areas allowed, and underwent surgical resection with histopathological correlation; the third declined surgery. Baseline ultrasound was unavailable, so findings were compared with the earliest 3-4-month follow-up. Response involved lesion shrinkage and loss of intratumoral blood flow. Serial imaging showed gradual resolution of hypoechoic nodules with vascularity on HFUS and blue-gray nests with arborizing vessels on dermoscopy, leaving avascular scar-like structures. Preoperative HFUS residual hypoechoic areas were correlated with histopathology, which showed chronic inflammatory infiltration (case 1) and mild dermal fibrosis (case 2), with no residual tumor. The third patient's malignant features regressed after six months. In this small case series, HFUS monitored deeper tissue changes after targeted therapy. In two histopathologically confirmed patients, complete imaging remission on HFUS plus dermoscopy corresponded to pathological complete response; however, given the small sample and histopathological confirmation in only two patients, this is a possible correspondence rather than evidence of true predictive capability. Post-treatment hypoechoic areas may reflect inflammation, fibrosis, or residual tumor, limiting specificity. Imaging-based complete response should be confirmed by biopsy or excision when feasible. Surgery remains the gold standard; non-surgical patients require close follow-up.

papers.abstract: Four-dimensional computed tomography (4D-CT)-guided functional-avoidance radiotherapy reduces radiation pneumonitis, but the lack of patient selection criteria limits its adoption. This study aimed to identify clinical predictors of lung ventilation heterogeneity and determine which patients derive the greatest dosimetric benefit from functional-avoidance planning. We retrospectively analyzed 274 lung cancer patients. 4D-CT ventilation imaging was generated via deformable registration and a density-change algorithm, and the coefficient of variation (CoV) across six lung zones quantified heterogeneity. Clinical factors were assessed using Mann-Whitney U, Spearman, and multivariable logistic regression for three ventilation outcomes. Thirty-two patients were selected from CoV quartiles and re-planned with functional-avoidance plans; dosimetric parameters were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied to address multiple comparisons. Univariate analysis showed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and airway obstruction reduced bilateral mean ventilation, while central tumors impaired ipsilateral ventilation. Higher CoV was observed in stage III-IV versus I-II, central versus peripheral tumors, and patients with airway obstruction. Multivariable analysis identified airway obstruction as an independent predictor of elevated CoV (adjusted OR = 2.914, 95% CI: 1.315-6.454, P<0.05). Central location and advanced stage showed borderline significance, while COPD trended toward lower CoV. Dosimetrically, functional-avoidance plans reduced functional lung metrics in a heterogeneity-dependent manner. After FDR correction, key metrics (fMLD, fV10, fV20, fV30) remained significant in Group 1 (highest CoV; Q = 0.040-0.049), while significance diminished in lower CoV groups. Leave-one-out (LOO) sensitivity analysis confirmed fMLD and fV20 as robust endpoints. Furthermore, beam arrangement modifications were most frequent in Group 1 (5/8 patients) and absent in Group 4 (0/8), reflecting clinical optimization needs rather than confounding. Ventilation heterogeneity is driven by tumor burden and airway patency. Patients with advanced stage, central tumors, or airway obstruction exhibit the strongest heterogeneity and may represent appropriate candidates for functional-avoidance radiotherapy in future prospective trials. However, as this replanning study lacked clinical follow-up for radiation pneumonitis, these findings reflect dosimetric rather than confirmed clinical patient-level benefit. Notably, CoV quartiles were derived from internal median splits within this cohort and require external validation. This study provides a dosimetric basis for hypothesis-generating patient selection.

papers.abstract: Immune-mediated liver injury caused by checkpoint inhibitors (ILICI) differs from chemotherapy- or targeted drug-related hepatotoxicity in pathogenesis and management. Biomarkers to distinguish ILICI from other anticancer agent-induced liver injuries are lacking. We compared the clinicopathological features, treatments, and outcomes of ILICI versus other anticancer agent-related liver injuries to identify distinguishing biomarkers. We retrospectively included patients with liver injury during anticancer therapy at Fujian Cancer Hospital between June 2022 and November 2024. Cases were classified as ILICI or non-ILICI using the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events v5.0 and the Roussel Uclaf Causality Assessment Method. Sixty-seven patients were enrolled, including 30 ILICI and 37 non-ILICI. ILICI was associated with more high-grade liver injury than non-ILICI (P = 0.001), with similar latency, recovery time, and prognosis. Corticosteroids were administered in 70% of ILICI vs. 5.4% of non-ILICI patients (P 30% in LSECs, lymphocytes, and KCs discriminated ILICI with an AUC of 0.811 (95%CI: 0.641-0.980). Sensitivity analyses and Firth penalized logistic regression confirmed that this finding remained robust after adjustment for confounders including pre-biopsy corticosteroid use and inactive HBV carrier status. ILICI was associated with more severe hepatic inflammatory necrosis and a greater need for immunosuppressive therapy than non-ILICI. The PD-L1 positivity rate >30% in LSECs, lymphocytes, and KCs may serve as a potential diagnostic biomarker for ILICI.

papers.abstract: Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) combined with lenvatinib and tislelizumab has shown potential activity in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but early treatment failure (ETF) remains common. We developed an exploratory model to estimate ETF, defined as radiologically confirmed progressive disease (PD) or all-cause death within 6 months after treatment initiation. This single-center retrospective study included advanced HCC patients treated with the triple regimen from June 2021 to June 2024. Baseline clinical, imaging, and hematological variables were analyzed. LASSO regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection. Restricted cubic splines assessed linearity, and λ.1se was examined as a sensitivity analysis. A multivariable logistic regression model was presented as a nomogram. Discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were evaluated, with 1000-resample bootstrap internal validation repeating the modeling pipeline. Among 118 patients, 33 (27.9%) experienced ETF; 28 had radiologically confirmed PD and 5 died without prior documented PD. At λ.min, LASSO selected maximum tumor diameter, Vp4 portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT), baseline systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), ALBI score, and log10-transformed alpha-fetoprotein (AFP). Under λ.1se, four predictors were retained, with SII excluded. The final model had an apparent ROC-AUC of 0.903 and an optimism-corrected ROC-AUC of 0.866. Calibration showed acceptable agreement between predicted and observed risks. DCA suggested net benefit over an exploratory threshold range of approximately 0.10-0.50, which should not be interpreted as a validated treatment-switching threshold. The nomogram showed promising internal discrimination for estimating 6-month ETF risk in advanced HCC patients receiving SBRT, lenvatinib, and tislelizumab. Given the modest sample size and single-center design, the model remains exploratory and hypothesis-generating. External multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation or use for treatment selection.

papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma carries a poor prognosis making its management challenging. Histotripsy is a non-invasive, non-ionizing, and non-thermal therapy that mechanically disrupts tumors through acoustic cavitation. We present the case of a 59-year-old man with locally advanced, multifocal, stage II intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma who achieved a complete pathologic response in the explanted liver after treatment with histotripsy and systemic drug therapy consisting of gemcitabine, cisplatin, durvalumab, and trastuzumab deruxtecan. This case highlights the potential role of noninvasive histotripsy as a bridging therapy to transplantation in selected patients with cholangiocarcinoma.

papers.abstract: To investigate tumor vascular habitat parameters based on dynamic susceptibility contrast-enhanced perfusion-weighted imaging (DSC-PWI) for differentiating glioblastoma (GBM) from solitary brain metastasis (SBM). In this single-center retrospective study, imaging data from 141 patients with pathologically or clinically confirmed malignant brain tumors (74 GBM, 67 SBM) were analyzed. The hemodynamic tissue signature (HTS) method was used to segment the lesions and construct four tumor vascular habitats: high angiogenic tumor (HAT), low angiogenic tumor (LAT), potentially infiltrated peripheral edema (IPE), and vasogenic peripheral edema (VPE). Pearson correlation analysis was used to quantify the correlations among habitat hemodynamic parameters. Habitat characteristic parameters were calculated, and ROC were plotted to evaluate the diagnostic performance. A nomogram model was constructed using logistic regression. GBM exhibited significantly higher median relative cerebral blood volume (rCBVmedian) and median relative cerebral blood flow (rCBFmedian) than SBM across all four habitat regions (all p < 0.001). In terms of volumetric parameters, the ratio of IPE volume to peritumoral volume (V (IPE)/V (P)) was significantly higher in the GBM group (p < 0.001). Among individual habitat parameters, LAT rCBFmedian showed the best diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.786 (95% CI: 0.709-0.850). In the GBM group, the perfusion parameters of the IPE and VPE were significantly positively correlated with those of the HAT, whereas no such correlation was found in the SBM group. A nomogram incorporating lesion location, enhancement pattern, and LAT-rCBFmedian yielded an AUC of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.79-0.92) for distinguishing GBM from SBM, with good calibration. Tumor vascular habitat parameters based on DSC-PWI demonstrate significant differences between newly diagnosed GBM and SBM, and the nomogram shows certain value in differentiating between the two tumor types.

papers.abstract: Frailty is associated with poor short-term surgical outcomes, but whether the Fried frailty phenotype is associated with long-term mortality after curative colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, independently of age and tumor stage, is uncertain. We examined this association using restricted mean survival time (RMST), which does not require proportional hazards. This retrospective multicenter cohort study included 304 patients aged ≥60 years who underwent curative CRC surgery at three centers in China in 2018-2019. The preoperative Fried phenotype was analyzed as robust (n=131), pre-frail (n=57), or frail (n=116); binary (robust versus non-robust) and ordinal codings were secondary. The primary outcome was 5-year all-cause mortality. Because proportional hazards were violated (Schoenfeld test P = 0.011), the RMST difference at 60 months was the primary effect measure, adjusted by pseudo-observation regression for age, sex, and TNM stage, the minimal adjustment set from a directed acyclic graph. Stage-specific and time-varying-effect analyses were also performed. Over a median follow-up of 60 months, 27 patients (8.9%) died. Five-year survival was 96.2%, 84.2%, and 88.8% in robust, pre-frail, and frail patients (log-rank P = 0.015). Unadjusted RMST differences versus robust patients were -2.38 months (95% CI -4.45 to -0.78) for pre-frail and -2.73 months (-4.58 to -1.09) for frail patients. After adjustment for age, sex, and TNM stage they were -1.48 months (-3.42 to 0.45; P = 0.13) and -0.81 months (-2.56 to 0.93; P = 0.36); for non-robust versus robust patients, -1.16 months (-2.50 to 0.19; P = 0.092). Estimates were in the same direction within every stage but imprecise. The hazard ratio for non-robust patients appeared higher in the first 36 months than later, but period-specific estimates were unstable and did not differ significantly (P = 0.15). The Fried frailty phenotype identified older patients with lower 5-year survival after curative CRC surgery. After adjustment for age and tumor stage the association was attenuated and imprecise, so an independent effect could not be established with 27 deaths. The apparent early concentration of excess mortality in non-robust patients is hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in larger cohorts with treatment and cause-of-death data.

papers.abstract: To analyze the correlation between inflammation, nutrition and metabolic indicators and the risk of papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and to construct and validate a nomogram for predicting PTC risk among patients with thyroid nodules undergoing surgery, to assist clinicians in making more individualized clinical decisions. Retrospective population-based cohort study. A retrospective study was conducted on the clinical medical records of patients with thyroid masses who underwent surgical treatment at Hebei General Hospital from 2020 to 2024. Independent risk factors for the onset of PTC were screened through Logistic regression analysis. A risk prediction model for the onset of PTC based on inflammatory, nutritional and metabolic indicators was constructed using R4.3.3 software and externally validated. A total of 1727 patients who underwent thyroidectomy for thyroid nodules were enrolled, among whom 1167 patients (67.6%) were pathologically-confirmed papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), and 560 patients (32.4%) had benign thyroid nodules after surgery. Multivariate logistic regression analysis demonstrated combined Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) (OR = 1.887, 95%CI: 1.174-3.031, P = 0.009), combined metabolic syndrome (MetS) (OR = 2.157, 95%CI: 1.449-3.211, P < 0.001), and elevated uric acid (UA) (OR = 1.640, 95%CI: 1.112-2.417, P = 0.013) were independent risk factors for PTC onset. Age ≥ 55 years (OR = 0.318, 95%CI: 0.238-0.424, P < 0.001), other marital status (OR = 0.067, 95%CI: 0.012-0.392, P = 0.003), and increased prognostic nutritional index (PNI) (OR = 0.934, 95%CI: 0.902-0.966, P < 0.001) were independent protective factors against PTC onset. Based on the above independent risk factors, a nomogram for PTC was constructed. The AUC of the ROC curve in the modeling group was 0.702, and that in the external validation group was 0.721, indicating that the nomogram has good predictive performance. The calibration curve and decision analysis curve also indicate that the nomogram has good predictive performance and clinical application efficacy. Combined HT, combined MetS, and elevated UA are independent risk factors for PTC onset, whereas age ≥ 55 years, other marital status, and PNI level represent independent protective factors.

papers.abstract: The Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) quantifies the inflammatory potential of diet. Evidence linking DII to prostate cancer remains limited and inconsistent. We evaluated the prospective association between DII and incident prostate cancer in a large population-based cohort. We included 30,972 men who were free of prostate cancer at baseline. The DII was derived from 27 dietary components assessed by the Oxford WebQ. Incident prostate cancer was identified from linked cancer-registry records (ICD-10 C61). Cox regression was the primary analysis, with age included in all adjusted models; logistic regression was secondary. Lag, additional-covariate, and age-stratified Cox models assessed sensitivity. Mediation and Mean Adequacy Ratio (MAR) analyses were exploratory. During a median follow-up of 13.8 years (IQR 13.5-14.2; 406,058 person-years), 1,546 participants developed incident prostate cancer. The unadjusted inverse association (HR per 1-unit DII increase 0.951, 95% CI 0.927-0.977) was attenuated after adjustment for age and other covariates (fully adjusted HR 0.986, 95% CI 0.956-1.018; P = 0.389; Q4 vs Q1 HR 0.928, 95% CI 0.788-1.093; P for trend = 0.426). The secondary logistic analysis was likewise null (OR per 1-unit increase 0.982, 95% CI 0.950-1.015; P = 0.275). Age-adjusted lag analyses and exploratory CRP/NLR mediation analyses did not materially alter this interpretation. DII was inversely correlated with the revised 18-nutrient MAR (Pearson r = -0.694; Spearman ρ = -0.756), but neither index was associated with prostate cancer in the age-adjusted joint model. An apparent inverse DII-prostate cancer association in unadjusted analyses was explained largely by age differences across DII categories. After adjustment for age and other covariates, neither logistic nor time-to-event analyses supported an independent association. These findings underscore the importance of rigorous age control in prostate cancer epidemiology and should not be interpreted causally.

papers.abstract: Urinary toxicities are common following prostate radiotherapy and can impair quality of life. New biomarkers are needed that can predict the risk of urinary toxicity following MRI guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MR-SBRT) to assist with selection of the most appropriate radiotherapy treatment approach. We aimed to identify urine miRNA biomarkers of radiation-induced urinary toxicities. Ten patients undergoing MR-SBRT were enrolled on a prospective biorepository protocol and urine specimens were collected before, at the final fraction and 2-4 months following radiotherapy. RNA was isolated and microRNA sequencing was performed followed by qPCR for confirmation of microRNA expression changes. Differences in microRNA expression were assessed with regard to timepoint, cancer risk category and urinary toxicity. Both sequencing and qPCR showed that expressions of miR-26a-5p and miR-95-3p decrease during MR-SBRT and increase during early follow up. miR-204-3p and miR-192-5p changed differently in patients with and without urinary radiation toxicity. Expression of miR-375-3p was lower in patients with higher risk category (NCCN unfavorable intermediate to high risk or recurrent/metastatic) at all timepoints and decreased during and after MR-SBRT, especially in patients with a lower risk category (NCCN low to favorable intermediate risk) of prostate cancer. Urine microRNA analysis is feasible and may identify biomarkers linked to radiation-induced urinary toxicity and prostate cancer severity. The findings of this pilot study are limited by the sample size and should be prospectively validated.

papers.abstract: Current preoperative assessment of meningioma brain invasion (BI) demands imaging analytical frameworks that optimize computational efficiency while capturing multidimensional tumor-pathology correlations. Building upon the inherent advantages of 2.5D MRI in synthesizing multiplanar biological data with manageable processing loads, this study innovatively integrates deep transfer learning (DTL), a technique bridging pretrained network knowledge with target domain adaptation, to systematically identify tumor-invasive biological signatures and develop an optimized predictive system using preoperative contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI). This retrospective study enrolled 674 patients with pathologically confirmed meningiomas, including 53 with BI and 621 without BI. The cohort was stratified into a training set and an independent test set. Tumor regions of interest (ROIs) were delineated on CE-T1WI, and radiomics and DTL features were extracted. Radiomics and DTL features were fused via early fusion, followed by feature selection. Within the training cohort, five-fold cross-validation was performed, with SMOTE applied exclusively to the training portion of each fold; validation folds and the independent test set retained their original class distributions. The effectiveness of the models was compared using the area under the ROC curve (AUC). In the training set, ComM achieved an AUC of 0.977, while in the test set, its AUC reached 0.935. ComM demonstrated the best performance (training set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCClinM > AUCDTLM; test set: AUCComM > AUCDTLRM > AUCRadM > AUCDTLM > AUCClinM), showing excellent preoperative predictive capability for meningioma BI. The Hosmer-Lemeshow test indicated good model fit, and the calibration curve revealed that ComM was closest to the ideal curve. ClinM, RadM, DTLM, DTLRM, and ComM based on 2.5D CE-T1WI all exhibited good performance in predicting meningioma BI. The clinical-radiomics-DTL fusion model (ComM) demonstrated the highest efficacy, suggesting that DTL provides additional features correlated with meningioma BI that differ from radiomics features. This model shows potential clinical utility for preoperative prediction; however, further external validation in larger multicenter cohorts is required before clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the predictive value of a nomogram incorporating ultrasound and clinical features for cervical lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with thyroid cancer. A retrospective analysis was conducted on patients pathologically diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) between April 2024 and January 2025. Radiomics features were extracted from two-dimensional thyroid ultrasound images, and feature selection was performed using the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO). Five classifiers were compared, and logistic regression was selected to construct the radiomics model. A clinical-radiomics model integrating the radiomics score and clinical predictors, together with a standalone clinical model, was developed using multivariable logistic regression. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated in a held-out internal validation set. Sex, Radscore, age, and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels were identified as independent predictors of CLNM in patients with PTC. Based on these variables, radiomics, clinical, and clinical radiomics models were constructed; the models achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.735, 0.792, and 0.867, respectively, in the validation set. DeLong's test and decision curve analysis (DCA) demonstrated that the clinical radiomics model outperformed the radiomics model in the validation set, offering a higher net clinical benefit. A nomogram integrating ultrasound imaging and clinical data effectively predicts the risk of CLNM in patients with PTC and may assist clinicians in developing individualized treatment strategies.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) has highly heterogeneous postoperative survival. Although contemporary prognostic assessment ideally requires molecular, functional, and surgical-detail variables, these data are often unavailable in population-based and multicenter real-world datasets. Adults with histologically recorded GBM and tumor-directed surgery (resection or biopsy) in SEER formed the derivation cohort. A multivariable Cox model estimated 6-, 12-, and 18-month overall survival and was externally evaluated in CGGA and an independent institutional cohort without refitting. Because extent of resection, biopsy details, performance status, MGMT promoter methylation, IDH status, and treatment-regimen details were unavailable or non-harmonizable, the model was explicitly intended for registry-based survival stratification when contemporary core prognostic variables are absent. The study included 3, 842 patients in the SEER derivation cohort, 512 in the CGGA validation cohort, and 96 in the institutional validation cohort. Age, marital status, year of diagnosis, tumor location, tumor size, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy were retained in the final model. The model showed acceptable discrimination and calibration in the derivation cohort and reproducible risk stratification in both validation cohorts. In the independent non-public institutional validation cohort, the 6-, 12-, and 18-month AUCs were 0.748, 0.721, and 0.694, respectively, with a Harrell's C-index of 0.708, supporting reproducible risk stratification in a real-world clinical patient cohort. This multicohort study developed a registry-compatible survival stratification model for surgically managed glioblastoma for GBM using routinely available variables. The model may support survival estimation under data-constrained conditions, but should not be interpreted as a comprehensive neuro-oncology prognostic system or treatment decision-support tool.

papers.abstract: Non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) is characterized by high recurrence rates, highlighting the need for effective, non-invasive diagnostic and risk stratification tools. Although urinary biomarkers are increasingly used worldwide, molecular data specific to Chinese NMIBC populations remain limited. This study explores the potential utility of TERT promoter and FGFR3 hotspot mutations detected in urinary tumor DNA (utDNA) in a prospective Chinese cohort. We prospectively enrolled 106 newly diagnosed NMIBC patients between February 2023 and August 2023 at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (ChiCTR2300076543). First-morning urine samples were collected prior to TURBT. A PCR-based UI-Seek assay was employed to detect hotspot mutations in the promoter region (M1: c.-146 C>T, C250T; M2: c.-124 C>T, C228T) and FGFR3 gene (M1: c.742 C>T, p.R248C; M2: c.746 C>G, p.S249C). The overall mutation rates for TERT promoter and FGFR3 were 49.06% and 15.09%, respectively, with a combined sensitivity of 55.66%. Compared with published study cohorts from Western countries and Japan, Chinese NMIBC patients showed differences in molecular mutation profiles. Notably, the TERT-M2 mutation was associated with tumor aggressiveness, with significant correlations observed for T1 stage (P = 0.011), high-grade tumors (P = 0.011), and high/very high EAU risk categories (P 24 months, n = 40) groups. T1 stage, high tumor grade, high/very high-risk stratification, and TERT mutations (especially the TERT-M2 subtype) were significantly associated with early recurrence (P 0.05). This study characterizes the mutational landscape of urinary tumor DNA (utDNA) in Chinese patients with non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). Our findings suggest that utDNA-based detection of TERT promoter mutations, particularly the M2 subtype, and FGFR3 mutations may provide complementary molecular information for recurrence risk assessment. Larger prospective multicenter studies are warranted to validate these findings and evaluate the clinical potential of utDNA as a non-invasive molecular tool in NMIBC management.

papers.abstract: Gallbladder polyps (GBPs) and colorectal neoplasia frequently coexist against a background of metabolic dysfunction. This study aimed to investigate the association between the Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index and high-risk colorectal adenoma (HRA) in patients with GBPs, and to evaluate the effect modification of gallbladder ultrasound characteristics on this association. This retrospective study included 620 patients with GBPs who underwent colonoscopy at Zhengzhou Central Hospital Affiliated to Zhengzhou University between 2022 and 2025. Patients were classified into no adenoma, non-high-risk adenoma (non-HRA), and HRA groups based on colonoscopic pathology. The Mantel-Haenszel linear trend test was used to assess the dose-response relationship between FIB-4 category and adenoma severity. Multivariable logistic regression was fitted with HRA as the outcome, adjusting for demographic and metabolic covariates. Sensitivity analysis was performed using FIB-4 as a continuous variable (per standard deviation increment). Prespecified subgroup analyses and multiplicative interaction models were conducted, with Wald and likelihood ratio tests (LRTs) evaluating the effect modification of gallbladder wall thickness on the FIB-4-HRA association. The FIB-4 category showed a dose-response relationship with adenoma severity (trend P = 0.0039). The risk of HRA in the high FIB-4 group was elevated in the unadjusted model (OR 5.83, P < 0.001) but attenuated after adjustment (aOR 2.32, P = 0.129). The overall aOR per 1-standard deviation (SD) increase in FIB-4 was 1.09 (P = 0.41). Subgroup analysis revealed that the association between per-1-SD increase in FIB-4 and HRA was present only among patients with gallbladder wall thickening (≥3 mm) (aOR = 6.38, P = 0.003), with no significant association in those with normal wall thickness (aOR = 0.94, P = 0.75). The multiplicative interaction term between FIB-4 and gallbladder wall thickness was significant (Wald P = 0.008, LRT P = 0.001). Subgroup analyses of this study showed that among patients with GBPs and gallbladder wall thickening, elevated FIB-4 was associated with an increased risk of high-risk colorectal adenoma. This association still requires validation in independent external cohorts.

papers.abstract: Computed tomography (CT)-derived vertebral attenuation has been recognized as an indicator of prognosis for patients undergoing tumor removal, liver transplant, or transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) therapy, but similar research has not been reported in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). This study aims to explore the prognostic value of CT-derived vertebral attenuation in HCC patients treated with ICIs. This retrospective study included HCC patients who received ICI treatment at Wuhan Union Hospital between July 2020 and March 2024. CT-derived vertebral attenuation was assessed by measuring mean Hounsfield unit (HU) values in the center of the first lumbar vertebra (L1) on non-contrast CT scans. Based on the optimal cutoff value derived from X-tile software, patients were classified into the CT-derived L1 attenuation-low group (≤100 HU) and the CT-derived L1 attenuation-high group (>100 HU). A comparison of the baseline characteristics of the two groups was made, followed by a propensity score matching (PSM) analysis to balance the variables. The objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) were calculated for both groups, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox regression models were used to analyze overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). The cohort consisted of 357 patients, divided into the L1 attenuation-low group (n = 112) and the L1 attenuation-high group (n = 245). Among all patients, 30.0% (107/357) achieved complete or partial response. After PSM analysis, both groups contained 91 patients. The L1 attenuation-low group had shorter OS (hazard ratio [HR], 1.73; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-2.60; P = 0.008) and PFS (HR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.04-2.08; P = 0.030) than the L1 attenuation-high group. CT-derived L1 attenuation can stratify survival risk for HCC patients undergoing ICI treatment.

papers.abstract: Currently, whether surgical staging can confer a survival benefit in patients with cervical cancer remains controversial, and its efficacy is similarly uncertain across different subgroups. The primary aim of this study was to assess the efficacy of laparoscopic para-aortic and pelvic lymphadenectomy prior to chemoradiotherapy in patients with International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) stage IIB-IIIC cervical cancer. The secondary aim was to identify the main prognostic factors. A total of 396 patients were included in this retrospective study, 97 patients who underwent laparoscopic para-aortic and pelvic lymphadenectomy before chemoradiotherapy comprised the surgical staging group, and 299 patients who received chemoradiotherapy alone comprised the clinical staging group. Kaplan-Meier and log-rank methods were used to construct and compare progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) curves, respectively. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to identify independent prognostic factors. There were no statistically significant differences in PFS (p = 0.187) or OS (p = 0.490) between the two groups. The estimated 5-year PFS rates were 67.0% (95%CI, 56.9%-75.7%) in the surgical staging group and 73.6% (95%CI, 67.4%-78.7%) in the clinical staging group. The corresponding 5-year OS rates were 76.3% (95%CI, 66.0%-83.9%) and 78.6% (95%CI, 72.7%-83.2%), respectively. Subgroup analysis stratified by imaging lymph node status demonstrated comparable survival outcomes. Multivariate analysis identified adenocarcinoma, pelvic wall involvement, and imaging-positive lymph nodes as independent risk factors for PFS; adenocarcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma, pelvic wall involvement, and imaging-positive lymph nodes were independent predictors of OS. Laparoscopic para-aortic and pelvic lymphadenectomy before chemoradiotherapy was not associated with improved PFS or OS in this retrospective cohort, Tumor histology, pelvic wall involvement, and imaging-positive lymph nodes were the main prognostic factors.

papers.abstract: Middle-aged and older adults (MAOs; defined as individuals aged ≥40 years) account for the global cancer burden, contributing to 70-80% of cases. Characterizing cancer profiles in this demographic is essential for developing targeted prevention and treatment strategies to mitigate global impacts. Using Global Burden of Diseases (GBD) 2021 data, we analyzed incidence, prevalence, mortality and Disability-Adjusted Life Years (DALYs) for 31 cancers among MAOs (aged≥40) across 204 countries/21 regions(1990-2021). Trends were quantified via Joinpoint regression, and autoregressive integrated moving-average (ARIMA) models projected the burden through 2035. Risk attribution utilized population attributable fractions across Socio-demographic Index (SDI) quintiles. An order-independent Shapley decomposition attributed projected cancer incidence changes during 2021-2035 to population growth, aging, and age-specific incidence rate shifts. In 2021, MAOs accounted for 48,804,114 incident cases and 9,434,210 deaths. Females exhibited a 1.14-fold higher age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) than males, yet males had a higher age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR). Projections suggested a continued rise in cancer burden through 2035. Peak incidence occurred in ages 60-69 and the highest mortality in ages 70-79. Breast cancer was the main cancer in females; tracheal/bronchus/lung cancer in males. Tracheal/bronchus/lung cancer dominated mortality across all groups except middle-aged women (breast cancer). High-SDI regions bore the greatest burden, characterized by tracheal/bronchus/lung and colorectal cancers, while low-SDI regions shifted toward breast, cervical and stomach cancer. Risk factor analysis from 2010-2021 revealed rising metabolic risks, with high body mass index (BMI) and fasting plasma glucose-attributable DALYs increasing by 12.39% and 11.36% respectively, especially in high-SDI regions. Conversely, while most behavioral risks declined, smoking remained the leading risk factor, contributing over 60% to lung cancer DALYs. In low-SDI regions, behavioral drivers such as unsafe sex (accounting for >90% of cervical cancer risk) and air pollution remained the dominant persistent risks. This study, the first focusing on MAOs' global cancer burden, reveals heterogeneous patterns by age, gender, and SDI. Lung cancer was the leading cause of death (smoking as main risk). Metabolic risks rose in high-SDI regions, behavioral risks in low-SDI regions. In conclusion, MAOs' cancer burden will rise through 2035; region-specific precision strategies are essential.

papers.abstract: Missed treatment workdays can prolong overall treatment time and may reduce tumor control, yet routine audits often conflate weekends, statutory holidays, and departmentally accepted rest schedules with untreated institutional workdays. We quantified calendar-defined missed-workday gaps-inter-fraction intervals containing ≥1 untreated institutional workday after excluding routine rest days-among patients with first treatment between June 2021 and December 2025 who were linkable between the MOSAIQ radiotherapy information system and the institutional oncology database (1,319 patients; 1,342 episodes). A locked stratified sample of 100 algorithm-positive gaps underwent documentation-based chart review as unplanned relevant (UR) or planned/appropriate (PA). We analyzed linkage sensitivity, opportunity-adjusted site rates with patient-clustered confidence intervals (CIs), opportunity-offset Poisson generalized estimating equations (GEE) including calendar year, and episode-clustered phase GEE. Under the documentation-based chart-review rule, 92 of 100 algorithm-positive gaps were labeled UR (17 department/equipment; 75 patient-factor) and 8 PA. Gaps occurred in 638/1,342 episodes (47.5%; patient-level 48.0%). Linked versus unlinked prevalence was 48.2% versus 51.7% (absolute difference -3.4 percentage points, 95% CI -11.2 to 4.4; P = 0.435). Among subgroups with ≥50 episodes, head and neck had the highest prevalence (75.3%) and breast the lowest (41.3%); opportunity-adjusted rates were 5.63 (cluster-bootstrap 95% CI 4.76-6.52) versus 2.63 (2.36-2.92) per 100 opportunities. Opportunity-offset Poisson GEE with calendar year gave a head-and-neck versus breast incidence rate ratio (IRR) of 2.99 (95% CI 2.18-4.11). An exploratory phase GEE (29,763 intervals; 1,323 clusters) showed a late versus early odds ratio (OR) of 1.31 (95% CI 1.12-1.54; P = 0.0009; absolute rates 2.8% vs 3.6%); after site, year, and intent adjustment, the OR was 1.32 (95% CI 1.12-1.57). This operational audit of institutional workdays without recorded treatment-rather than clinically confirmed unplanned interruptions-shows frequent gaps after excluding routine rest. Most reviewed positives received patient-factor labels under a documentation rule. Calendar-aware auditing may support departmental monitoring; priority-based compensation remains a proposed application.

papers.abstract: Fecal incontinence (FI) is prevalent in critically ill oncology patients, frequently compounded by chemotherapy-induced diarrhea (CID) and severe thrombocytopenia. Conventional indwelling balloon catheters (IBCs), the standard approach to FI management in the ICU, generate intraluminal radial pressures that frequently exceed mucosal capillary perfusion thresholds and are formally contraindicated by manufacturers in patients with platelet counts below 50 x 109/L. This retrospective analysis and structured narrative literature review evaluates the safety, fecal containment efficacy, and nursing workload impact of a novel pressure-free automated stool management (ASM) system in high-risk oncology ICU patients. A retrospective analysis was conducted at a major academic comprehensive cancer center in the United States during 2025. Outcome data from 190 unique adult oncology ICU patients, including two structured evaluation cohorts of 20 patients each, followed by broader institutional implementation (n=150), were compiled from standardized nursing quality improvement product evaluation forms completed throughout each patient's device-use period. A prospectively designated thrombocytopenic subgroup (n=47; platelet counts <50 x 109/L at device deployment) was analyzed separately. A structured narrative literature review was conducted across PubMed, MEDLINE, and CINAHL (final search: February 2026). Across 190 unique device placements, zero device-related adverse events were observed (adverse event rate 0%; 95% CI upper bound 1.6%, rule of three). In the thrombocytopenic subgroup (n=47), zero device-related adverse events were observed (95% CI upper bound 6.4%). No device-related mucosal bleeding, perforation, ulceration, necrosis, or device malfunction requiring intervention was documented. The device achieved 100% successful fecal diversion, with no major leakage event (defined as stool output requiring linen replacement) recorded. The per-assessment leakage rate was 1.7% (11 positive assessments out of 646 total), all representing minor peripheral moisture requiring only topical hygiene management with no linen change. Daily nursing time with ASM was 6.8 minutes per patient per day; contextual comparison with published estimates of 120 minutes per patient per day (IBC protocol) and 174 minutes per patient per day (absorbent pad management) from Vargo et al. yields estimated differences of 94% and 96%, respectively, subject to methodological differences between datasets. Retrospective chart review identified no chemotherapy delays or ICU length of stay prolongation attributable to device-related complications. This early institutional experience with a novel pressure-free ASM across 190 unique oncology ICU placements, including 47 in patients with severe thrombocytopenia, was not associated with any observed device-related adverse event. These findings represent hypothesis-generating preliminary data and do not establish superiority over conventional devices. The clinical need for safe fecal management alternatives in thrombocytopenic oncology patients is substantive; these data provide rationale for appropriately powered prospective comparative trials.

papers.abstract: Evidence on prostate cancer (PCa) knowledge and PSA-related testing behavior in Palestine remains limited. We assessed general awareness, factual knowledge, willingness to undergo PSA testing if offered, reported prior PSA testing/prostate examination, and factors associated with prior testing. We conducted a cross-sectional online survey from 19 November to 21 December 2025 among adult men aged 18 years or older recruited from Palestinian communities. The full cohort comprised 1,047 consenting participants. The exported dataset contained two incompatible response formats for the 12 factual knowledge items; composite knowledge analyses were therefore limited to 568 respondents with complete, unambiguous single Yes/No responses. Knowledge was scored from 0 to 12 using the study answer key. Willingness and prior testing were analyzed as binary outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression assessed factors associated with prior testing. Mean age was 28.7 ± 12.4 years and 78.6% were aged 18-39 years. Overall, 80.0% had heard of PCa, 26.1% had heard of PSA testing, 31.2% were willing to undergo PSA testing if offered, and 5.6% reported prior PSA testing and/or prostate examination. Among the 568 scorable knowledge respondents, mean knowledge was 7.07 ± 1.84 of 12 and 89.1% had limited knowledge (<80% correct); KR-20 was 0.235. Adequate knowledge was associated with lower willingness (12.9% vs 32.8%; p=0.002) but not prior testing (3.2% vs 6.1%; p=0.526). In the full cohort, older age (aOR 1.08 per year; 95% CI 1.05-1.10), healthcare background (aOR 2.10; 95% CI 1.17-3.77), and first-degree family history (aOR 2.22; 95% CI 1.01-4.86) were independently associated with prior testing. Among never-tested participants, the leading reported barriers were low perceived personal risk (55.3%) and lack of physician/healthcare-provider recommendation (43.1%); multiple responses were allowed. In this predominantly young online sample, general awareness exceeded detailed factual knowledge, while willingness and reported prior testing were low. The divergence between knowledge and behavior should be interpreted cautiously because knowledge analyses used a restricted subset and the shortened scale had low internal consistency. Findings support culturally appropriate, risk-adapted clinician-patient communication and further validation of locally adapted measurement tools.

papers.abstract: Autologous breast reconstruction restores breast volume and contour after mastectomy, but reconstruction of the nipple-areola complex remains central to the perception of breast completeness. Traditionally, nipple reconstruction has been delayed until the reconstructed breast mound has stabilized, allowing the final nipple position and projection to be adjusted after soft-tissue settling and scar remodeling. However, in selected patients undergoing autologous reconstruction, simultaneous nipple reconstruction can be integrated into breast shaping, thereby reducing additional procedures, avoiding a second local incision and making use of redundant skin and soft tissue that would otherwise be discarded during flap tailoring. This strategy also allows surgeons to plan breast contour, nipple position, projection and symmetry as a single three-dimensional aesthetic unit. Nevertheless, accurate intraoperative positioning, reliable perfusion and durable long-term projection remain major technical challenges. In this case-based narrative review, we discuss the rationale, potential advantages, patient selection and limitations of immediate nipple reconstruction during autologous breast reconstruction. We further present three representative approaches from our center: a local flap, a pedicled perforator-based flap and a free perforator-based flap. These cases suggest that immediate nipple reconstruction should not be regarded as a single standardized operation, but as a flexible reconstructive strategy that should be tailored to tissue availability, vascular anatomy and aesthetic goals.

papers.abstract: Developing peripheral blood-based diagnostic models for idiopathic Parkinson's disease (iPD), particularly those leveraging the T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, has long been considered infeasible because patient-derived TCRs appear to lack convergent sequence motifs. We reasoned that this apparent absence of shared TCR features likely reflects both insufficient sample sizes and unaccounted immune heterogeneity within the iPD population. We reconstructed TCR repertoires from the two largest iPD cohorts currently available, anchoring them with three mechanistically distinct mouse models to stratify patients into model-anchored informed subtypes. Within these data-driven subtypes, we trained subtype-specific, multimodal multi-instance classifiers. We demonstrated that iPD patients can be successfully stratified into model-anchored informed subtypes. Furthermore, the trained subtype-specific, multimodal multi-instance classifiers achieved an Area Under Curve (AUC) exceeding 0.8 for both subtypes. Our findings underscore the critical role of disease stratification in enabling TCR repertoire-based modeling in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.abstract: Environmental exposures such as air pollution may influence human health partly through microbiome, but statistical modeling is challenged by spatial dependence across regions and ecological correlations among taxa. We propose SpaMixed, a novel spatial mixed modeling framework for microbiome count data that incorporates both sources of dependence using conditional autoregressive priors. In simulations, SpaMixed achieved high feature selection power while maintaining low false positive rates and reduced estimation error relative to existing methods. Applied to two real studies with fine particulate matter (PM2.5) exposures, SpaMixed identified biologically plausible PM2.5-associated taxa, supporting its utility for environmental microbiome research.

papers.abstract: The biosynthesis of bacterial aromatic polyketides (type II polyketides, T2PKs) employs a single set of catalysts (ketosynthases, KSs or KSα, with chain length factors, CLFs or KSβ) and iteratively assembles a carbon backbone with precise chain length control. Considering the increasing number of T2PKs discovered in laboratory settings, it is necessary to understand the evolutionary trajectories of KSs and CLFs. We employ our recently developed algorithm, MAAPE, based on large protein language model to glean insights into the evolution process of KSs and CLFs. Our findings indicate the evolutionary history of KS and CLF domains from bacterial T2PKSs and identify a shared ancestral cluster (Cluster A), supporting a common origin. Despite structural homology, KSs and CLFs followed distinct evolutionary paths, shaped by coevolution and early horizontal gene transfer. Understanding the evolutionary lineage of these enzymes will illuminate the natural optimization processes of their functions and present opportunities for the rational design of novel polyketides with enhanced efficacy.

papers.abstract: Epigenetic reprogramming underlies innate immune memory. However, whether trained immunity can be induced via epigenetic intervention to combat tumors, and the key regulators controlling this process, remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that histone deacetylase inhibitor (HDACi) priming establishes a trained immunity-like state in monocytes/macrophages, conferring potent antitumor effect in multiple models of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) in female mice. Interferon regulatory factor 8 (IRF8) is identified as the master regulator of the inflammatory transcriptional program, which is governed by IRF8-associated super-enhancers and reinforced by HDACi. Myeloid-specific IRF8 deficiency impairs pro-inflammatory macrophage differentiation and abrogates HDACi-induced antitumor efficacy. Moreover, an IRF8-driven, CCL8-expressing macrophage subset recruits and activates cytotoxic CCR5+CD8+ T cells in the TNBC microenvironment. As a proof-of-principle with translational relevance, CCL8-overexpressing EGFR-targeted CAR T cells exhibit enhanced trafficking and improved efficacy in a humanized TNBC model. Our study defines the IRF8-CCL8-CCR5 axis as an epigenetically potentiated nexus of innate and adaptive antitumor immunity.

papers.abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF), caused by CFTR mutations, is characterized by progressive pulmonary remodeling, particularly during bacterial infection. This pathological environment, exacerbated by altered epithelial growth, leads to thickened airway walls, inducing permanent narrowing and long-term breathing difficulties. However, what drives this adverse milieu remains unclear. Here, we identify activation of the de novo pathway of pyrimidine synthesis (DNPPS) as a central contributor of CF lung remodeling. In response to impaired mitochondrial bioenergetics, CFTR-mutant epithelial cells engage compensatory DNPPS activity, functionally coupling mitochondrial oxidative metabolism to pyrimidine production and, inadvertently, promoting proliferation. This phenotype is reversible with CFTR modulators and pharmacologic DNPPS inhibitors using clinically established agents. Strikingly, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the predominant CF pathogen, undergoes convergent pyrimidine adaptation, activating its own DNPPS machinery to amplify biomass and sustain a remodeled niche. Together, these findings define pyrimidine metabolism as a shared host-pathogen axis driving epithelial restructuring and bacterial persistence in the CF lung.

papers.abstract: Orbital Hall effects have recently attracted significant attention for generating substantial orbital angular momentum currents in both strong- and weak-spin-orbit-coupling materials. Despite extensive theoretical and experimental progress on the orbital Hall effect, its thermal counterpart, in which a temperature gradient drives a transverse orbital current, known as the orbital Nernst effect, has remained experimentally elusive. Here, we report the first experimental evidence for the orbital Nernst effect by measuring the magneto-thermopower in the yttrium iron garnet (YIG)/Pt/CuOx heterostructures. Through systematic comparison with the YIG/Pt and YIG/CuOx heterostructures, we show that both the magneto-thermopower and the magnetoresistance for YIG/Pt/CuOx are markedly enhanced due to the contributions from the orbital Nernst effect and the orbital Hall effect in CuOx, respectively. Our experimental evidence for the orbital Nernst effect supports the orbital degree of freedom as a promising route for heat-energy harvesting and orbital angular momentum thermal transport in earth-abundant materials.

papers.abstract: Extreme temperatures pose severe risks for population health and healthcare systems. However, little research has examined implications for incarcerated populations, who may be particularly vulnerable given their limited control over their thermal environments. Here, we show that among people imprisoned in Pennsylvania (2000-2023), both warmer and cooler temperatures were significantly associated with higher rates of mortality, transfers to outside medical facilities and prison infirmary admissions, relative to outcome-specific reference minimum threshold temperatures. As temperature extremes become more frequent and severe, policy action including decarceration and the provision of accessible prison healthcare is urgently needed to protect the health of incarcerated populations.

papers.abstract: Specimen preparation is a critical and rate-limiting step in cryo-EM structural analysis, primarily due to challenges posed by the air-water interface. In this study, we introduce carbon nanotubes (CNTs) as a one-dimensional fibrous support material to address this issue. CNTs interact with macromolecules, effectively protecting them from air-water interfaces, and macromolecules arrange themselves around CNTs in various orientations. Furthermore, CNTs biofunctionalized with affinity tags exhibit strong specificity in binding target macromolecules, facilitating direct purification of targets from cell lysates and on-grid assembly of complexes for subsequent cryo-EM analysis. We also demonstrate that CNT grids are compatible with cell culturing, allowing for seamless integration into the cryo-EM characterization workflow for cellular structures. We anticipate that these properties will make the CNT network a promising support for cryo-EM.

papers.abstract: Ferroelectric flux-closures are promising candidates for high-performance memories, offering reversible switching and low power consumption. However, integration of ferroelectric flux-closures into memory devices is elusive, mostly due to the constraint from the substrate on which polar film is grown. Here, we demonstrate ferroelectric field-effect transistors (Fe-FETs) based on freestanding films with identical polar flux-closures. The retention of flux-closure in the freestanding film is driven by the intrinsic self-organization of polarization to minimize the combined elastic and electrostatic energies. The flux-closure structures exhibit low coercive electric field (Ec), negligible leakage currents, and endurance up to 1010 cycles. Furthermore, the as-fabricated complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS)-compatible Fe-FET arrays achieve reversible information writing and erasure. They set a benchmark for perovskite-structured devices by simultaneously achieving a large memory window of 0.43 V/nm and a high on/off ratio of 108, while maintaining endurance and stability. Our work paves the way for ferroelectric devices in future semiconductor industries.

papers.abstract: The bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) in polar crystals offers a promising way to surpass the energy-conversion limits of conventional p-n junction devices. In layered materials, BPVE is typically dominated by an out-of-plane component. However, strong in-plane performance is essential for planar photovoltaics, requiring innovative strategies to overcome fundamental material constraints. In this study, an innovative pressure-induced emergence of in-plane BPVE is demonstrated in the planar-nonpolar layered bulk semiconductor γ-type indium selenide. External pressure distorts the lattice and breaks the intrinsic threefold rotational symmetry, triggering in-plane photovoltaic responses that are otherwise symmetry-forbidden at ambient pressure. Furthermore, the in-plane BPVE shows a distinctive crystallographic orientation dependence: the photocurrent is significantly higher along the armchair direction than along the zigzag direction, with a large anisotropy ratio of up to 280 observed at 0.16 GPa. Experimental characterization and first-principles calculations reveal that pressure lifts the symmetry-protected planar nonpolarity, reconstructing the electronic structure and activating a sizable in-plane shift-current response that is forbidden at ambient pressure. More broadly, this work establishes symmetry engineering through pressure as a general strategy for achieving large in-plane bulk photovoltaic responses in layered systems, without relying on material nanostructuring or interfacial design.

papers.abstract: Protein kinase CK2 plays an important role in the regulation of metabolism and obesity. However, the metabolic role of CK2 and its substrates in the brain remain largely unknown. Here, we show that microglial CK2 is required for metabolic homeostasis through ASC phosphorylation and subsequent NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated interleukin (IL)-18 maturation and release. Mice with microglia-specific, inducible deletion of CK2 regulatory subunit β (CK2β) showed obese phenotypes with weight gain, abnormal glucose homeostasis, and decreased energy expenditure. At the molecular level, CK2 phosphorylated ASC at T154, and this phosphorylation was essential for ASC aggregation and NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Microglial deletion of CK2β decreased central production of IL-18, mirroring the obese phenotypes of mice lacking IL-18 signaling. Our results suggest that the microglial CK2-ASC-NLRP3 axis underlies the central regulation of metabolic homeostasis and prevents obesity through processing and secretion of IL-18. Nevertheless, a gap remains between these molecular mechanistic findings and the observed in vivo behavioral and metabolic phenotypes, highlighting the need for future systems-level analyses to fully delineate the broader substrate landscape of CK2 and to integrate the functional outcomes of CK2 deficiency in microglia with in vivo phenotypes.

papers.abstract: The optical frequency comb has made a significant impact in precision spectroscopy and on our ability to probe atomic, molecular and, recently, nuclear transitions to further our understanding of their fundamental properties and how their dynamics and complex interactions affect the observed world. To expand the energy scales and types of systems that can be studied, frequency comb sources from terahertz to vacuum ultraviolet frequencies and beyond have been pursued. Dual-comb spectroscopy, enabled by the development of these frequency comb sources, allows broadband absorption measurements of complicated spectra, exceeding the limitations of direct, single-comb spectroscopy. To date, however, the dual-comb approach has not been able to directly access many important transitions that lie at challenging vacuum ultraviolet wavelengths. Here, we demonstrate dual-comb spectroscopy in the vacuum ultraviolet utilizing intracavity high harmonic generation. This multi-harmonic source is used to measure molecular absorbance spectra at λ = 210 nm and λ = 149 nm from room-temperature samples of acetylene and ammonia, respectively. These measurements resolve the Doppler broadened structure of congested molecular spectra with absolute frequency accuracy. Noise contributions to the vacuum ultraviolet dual-comb spectroscopy measurements are characterized, guiding future efforts and technological development in this region.

papers.abstract: The TREK two-pore domain potassium channels regulate membrane excitability and respond to diverse physiological stimuli. Single-site mutations of TREK are associated with neurodevelopmental disorders and can cause pathological channel hyperactivation. Here, using the OneOPES enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics framework, we characterize the energetics of conformational transition along a predefined pathway connecting the up and down states of TREK-2, together with initial conformational rearrangements of the selectivity filter under physiological stimuli and disease-mimicking conditions. The simulations reveal a shared energetic axis coupling the lower helices, proximal C-terminus, and selectivity filter to govern channel gating. Predicted conformational effects of a disease-mimicking mutation were validated electrophysiologically using a conformation-sensitive TREK-2 inhibitor. Together with our previous unbiased MD simulations, these results establish an energetic framework for TREK-2 regulation and dysfunction, complementing prior structural and mechanistic studies while highlighting the potential and methodological challenges of advanced enhanced-sampling approaches for resolving complex conformational landscapes of ion channels.

papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxins (BoNTs) are potent bacterial toxins. Distinct BoNT-like toxins, including BoNT/X, BoNT/En, and PMP1, form a distinct lineage. Here we characterize two additional members of this group, PG-toxin 1 and 2 (PG1 and PG2). Their light-chain (LC) and heavy-chain (HC) domains are encoded by adjacent genes. PG1 and PG2 LCs cleave Drosophila SNAP-25 at distinct sites (N196-E197 and R191-K193, respectively); PG1 is more potent, while PG2 activity depends on pH and ionic strength. Both LCs enter Sf9 cells via clathrin-mediated endocytosis. PG1 LC is toxic to Drosophila and northern armyworm independently of its HC, whereas PG2 LC toxicity is enhanced by its HC. Cryo-EM shows that PG1 adopts a distinct compact di-chain architecture with a door-hinge-like "belt." These findings expand the structural and functional diversity of the BoNT family and support the potential of PG-toxins as insecticidal agents and research tools.

papers.abstract: The United Nations has committed to halting and reversing biodiversity loss by 2030. Despite this commitment, mining remains a major driver of biodiversity decline, particularly in conservation priority zones (CPZs) and areas with high species extinction risk. Regardless of growing awareness, the full extent of current and future mining threats to biodiversity remains inadequately quantified, limiting effective global conservation strategies. Here, we quantify the threats of 145,000 km² of current mining land to biodiversity. We find that 34% (49,000 km²) of these mining areas overlap with CPZs, intersecting the ranges of more than 2,300 species, including many classified as threatened. These threats span 14 biomes, with disproportionately high relative impacts in fragile ecosystems such as Mangroves and the Mediterranean. Furthermore, an additional 43% (12 million km²), 29% (2 million km²), and 37% (4 million km²) of land potentially exploitable for metals, non-metals, and coal, respectively, overlap with CPZs, highlighting the heightened risks from future mining expansion without consideration for biodiversity. Our findings offer actionable insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders, guiding conservation efforts to mitigate biodiversity loss and align mining practices with global conservation goals, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals and the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

papers.abstract: The downscaling of silicon field-effect transistors is approaching fundamental limits, with the international roadmap for devices and systems (IRDS) projecting a 12 nm channel length plateau by 2037. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors have emerged as promising candidates for extended transistor scaling. However, no experimental demonstration has thus far surpassed the fundamental switching limits of advanced silicon. Here, we report monolayer MoS₂ transistors with physical channel lengths below 5 nm, achieving a subthreshold swing of 88 mV/dec and an on/off ratio above 106. These results surpass both the theoretical subthreshold limit of silicon and state-of-the-art emerging semiconductors-based transistors at comparable dimensions. To ensure high throughput, we develop a photolithography based, complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) compatible process and demonstrate 4-inch wafer-scale integration. We implement a design-technology co-optimization approach featuring an air-gap isolation and gate-contact overlap design to effectively suppress short channel effects. This work demonstrates subthreshold transport in a 2D semiconductor transistor beyond the silicon limit, showing a viable pathway for extending transistor scaling and energy-efficient computing.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background The acute inpatient symptom state following oesophagectomy is multidimensional and heterogeneous. However, the structure, between-patient heterogeneity, and network features of symptoms remain incompletely characterised. Method We analysed 1047 postoperative patients with oesophageal cancer from four hospitals in Anhui Province, China, in the “Be Resilient to Oesophageal Cancer” program. We applied principal component analysis to summarise symptom dimensions and latent profile analysis to derive patient groups of symptom burden. Symptom networks were estimated and centrality computed to identify candidate targets. We then performed in silico node-perturbation simulations to estimate potential system-level effects of alleviating versus aggravating individual symptoms. Results Four symptom dimensions emerged from the principal component analysis: somatic discomfort and fatigue, psychological distress, social functioning impairment, and gastrointestinal/appetite-related symptoms. A low-burden group (80.2%) and a high-burden group (19.8%) were identified. The overall network’s most central symptom was “reduced social interaction” ( r = 2.52). Within groups, “worry” was most central in the low-burden group ( r = 2.08), whereas “incision pain” was most central in the high-burden group (r=2.56). Computer simulations revealed that, within alleviating interventions, somatic symptoms accounted for the highest proportion across all symptom types (incision pain: −20.68% to −9.17%). Conversely, within aggravating interventions, psychosocial symptoms constituted the largest share in both the overall symptom network and the low-burden group (helplessness: 24.13% to 30.27%), whereas somatic symptoms dominated the high-burden group (incision pain: 9.17%). Conclusion A multimethod pipeline identified reduced social interaction, worry, and incision pain as profile-specific, structurally prominent symptoms within the postoperative day 3 symptom networks. These findings highlight distinct psychosocial and somatic features across symptom-burden profiles and provide hypotheses for subsequent longitudinal and interventional studies.

papers.abstract: Phyllodes tumors (PTs) can overlap with fibroadenomas clinically and radiologically, and incomplete preoperative characterization can alter surgical planning. We describe three women with borderline or malignant PTs who declined preoperative core needle biopsy; clinical underestimation of malignancy also contributed to proceeding directly to excision. Case 1, a 36-year-old woman with long-standing bilateral masses, had a 63-mm malignant PT with heterologous chondroid and osseous differentiation and osteoclast-like giant cells; two contralateral lesions were fibroadenomas. An involved margin prompted re-excision, with no residual tumor and a final closest histological margin of 20 mm, permitting breast conservation. Case 2, a 68-year-old woman with a 75-mm malignant PT, had mildly prominent ipsilateral axillary nodes on mammography but no abnormal enlargement on axillary ultrasonography. Following malignant PT interpretation on frozen section, wide local excision was converted to total mastectomy; sentinel lymph node biopsy was negative (0/3), and the closest margin was the deep margin at 20 mm. The patient declined postoperative radiotherapy. Case 3, a 53-year-old woman with previous right breast fibroadenoma excision, had a right borderline PT involving the inked margin and contralateral pseudoangiomatous stromal hyperplasia. Re-excision approximately 2 cm beyond the previous surgical margin found no residual tumor. All three patients had satisfactory postoperative wound healing, with no reported complications or recurrence during the reported 6-month follow-up. These cases highlight the need for preoperative tissue diagnosis, attention to discrepant axillary imaging, individualized margin-directed surgery, and long-term surveillance.

papers.abstract: Objective To systematically evaluate published nomograms developed for patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) treated with radiotherapy, focusing on prognostic performance, core predictive variables, and implications for future model development. Methods A systematic literature search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library identified studies published between 2010 and 2025 that developed new nomograms for LACC cohorts treated with radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy. Data extraction included study population, predicted outcomes (overall survival [OS], progression-free survival [PFS], or disease-free survival [DFS]), model performance (C-index), validation methods, calibration, and predictor variables. Predictor patterns were summarized primarily by frequency of inclusion across nomograms, with β-coefficients used only for exploratory within-model descriptions. Results Nine studies met the inclusion criteria; eight developed nomograms for OS and three evaluated disease progression outcomes (PFS or DFS), with two studies evaluating both outcome categories. Reported C-indices ranged from 0.68 to 0.835, indicating moderate to good discrimination. Lymph node status, FIGO stage, and tumor size were among the most frequently incorporated predictors, while histology and SCC-Ag were also recurrently included. Validation in independent cohorts remained limited. Graphical calibration was commonly reported, whereas quantitative calibration measures and decision-curve analyses were inconsistently reported. Conclusions Nomograms for LACC treated with radiotherapy generally demonstrate moderate-to-good discriminative performance and frequently incorporate lymph node status, stage, and tumor size. However, methodological heterogeneity, incomplete validation, and evolving treatment paradigms limit their immediate generalizability. Future work should focus on robust external validation, recalibration, and evaluation in contemporary treatment cohorts before clinical implementation.
